theme: identity, posture-as-identity, human identity and EUD
owner_ambition: Originated by the owner in one morning, 2026-07-31, as a widening of graded enforcement. (1) 09:30 — "what sort of things could we extend this to be so its less a go/no-go decision, but more colour than that". (2) 09:37 — "we should encourage least privilage and zero trust... so we also need to think about the policy being a baked in identity attribute for the running services, so that its an attestation/property on the service accou[nt] credetntials that they get, is this an openbao/istio/type thing?", framed cross-org from the outset ("the customer accounts reset service in a org might say it only supports the current version of the policy to talk to it"). (3) 09:44 — "SPIFFE/SPIRE" as the carrier. (4) 09:59 — "this is all just 'the policy'". (5) 10:11 — "where does human identity fit in? can we also think about eud handling in order to consider the whole big picture". (6) 10:30 — "primary demo rig is the mac, go with Secure-Enclave-key-live, whats the answers for windows euds?"; 10:34 "does utm give windows a tpm in a vm on my mac?"; 10:38 "lets go with real mac, and build everything to demo with the vtpm and narrate in demo that its virtual but point carries". (7) 2026-08-05 09:30 — "signatures also contain attestations about their runtime, model versions, configurations etc and can provide attestation of the human involvement (preferably lack of human, so that its like a ci build artifact being signed by ci)". Later evolution this layer must honour: 2026-08-19 "2 split everything. We are demonstrating a multi org thing" and "the financial risk of 21707 doesn't seem sane to the same on every org, its proporiate to the org right?"; 2026-08-20 "you're always caged even if it's a permissive one. It's the spec of the cage that can change" / "nothing runs without a cage even if they're permissive"; 2026-08-22 "there is no real gate anymore. Just cages"; 2026-08-25 "goes in all the repos its supposed to go in" and "Make sure that we're covering all of the features that we built in the work recently. the whole lot." Standing rules: "build everything", "nothing is a nice to have", Flux integral unless disproven.
what_was_specified: Only in .scratch/talk-spec. map.md:152-171 carries the model in three paragraphs: "(B) posture-as-identity: the policy version becomes a claim on the workload's SPIFFE/SPIRE SVID, gating Istio authz + OpenBao secrets"; "generalises to three actor classes: workload · human · device, one SPIFFE + gitsign root"; "Mac Secure-Enclave key = the genuine live root, Windows/Linux via UTM vTPM VMs (built full, narrated virtual)"; "Not Teleport". Six build tickets: 14 identity plane, 15 Kyverno→SPIRE posture projection, 16 currency controller, 17 posture-gated reach+secrets, 18 human+device access plane, 19 posture-gated human access, 20 EUD vTPM VMs. Two research issues (talk-spec/issues/17, /19). DECISION_AUDIT P180 records the carrier choice; P089 the trust-anchor location. Beyond that, nothing: no ADR in docs/adr/ (0001-0018 exist, none on identity, trust domains, actor classes or attestation carriers), no CONTEXT.md domain entry for SPIFFE/SPIRE/EUD/device (posture appears only as the de-postured runtime state), and none of the four post-Aug-19 efforts (multi-org-estate, govern-what-you-dont-control, computed-semver, policy-composition) opened a ticket to re-fit this layer to the six-org split, the cage model or computed semver.
what_was_built: Real and running-capable on ONE cluster (kind-driftwood) and ONE trust domain (acme.internal). platform/identity: SPIRE (server, agent, controller-manager, CSI driver, OIDC provider), Istio consuming SPIRE via the documented Workload-API-socket integration, mesh-wide STRICT mTLS, OpenBao dev mode, a ping/pong pair proving SPIFFE-principal authz — all Flux HelmReleases. Three genuinely live-discovered bugs found and fixed with regression asserts (SPIRE chart 0.24.0 value renames; istiod ENABLE_CA_SERVER=false breaking the injector webhook; ClusterSPIFFEID.className omission leaving both CRDs silently unreconciled since day one). platform/posture: Kyverno MutatingPolicy stamping posture.acme.io/version from the validated claim and clobbering forgery, ValidatingPolicy denying a mismatch, ClusterSPIFFEID baking posture/<v> as the leading SVID segment — kyverno-test-proven offline, live-proven 2026-08-20 (a real pod held spiffe://acme.internal/posture/2.0.0/ns/tuppence-reset/sa/teller-current). platform/currency-controller: a per-minute CronJob (pure-stdlib urllib) reading the live flux-operator ResourceSet and de-posturing stale pods. tuppence/reset: Istio AuthorizationPolicy on the posture prefix, live-proven both ways (current 200, stale 403); OpenBao jwt role on the same prefix, never live-proven. platform/access: real Pomerium Core + Dex charts, tpm_devid SPIRE overlay, device ClusterStaticEntry, access.py graded ALLOW/STEP_UP/DENY. platform/break-glass: break-glass.py, genuinely importing fair.py and access.py, adding a CAGE rung priced from FAIR TVaR £. platform/eud: two vTPM VM specs, real qcow2 disks, an enrolment template, an honest WHfB runbook. Absent anywhere: a second trust domain, SPIFFE federation, any identity/posture object on the tuppence or ludlow clusters, a completed device attestation (every selector is REPLACE_WITH_ATTESTED_TPM_FINGERPRINT), a booted EUD VM (ISO paths are placeholders), a Pomerium signing key (signingKey: ""), external-authz wiring to either graded engine, a tier segment on any SVID, and any cage or version claim on the identity substrate's own pods. Live state 2026-08-27 (scratchpad/live/talk-verify-live.json): spire-agent CrashLoopBackOff 398 restarts, spire-spiffe-oidc-discovery-provider Unknown 56 restarts, six currency-controller Job pods in Error (HTTP 404 from urllib), and talk/up.sh names "platform: posture projection" and "platform: graded enforcement envelope (cages)" as degraded layers.

findings.title: One trust domain, one cluster: the multi-org split never reached the identity layer
findings.claim: Every SPIFFE identity in the estate is minted by a single SPIRE server on kind-driftwood under the single trust domain acme.internal, and tuppence's flagship posture-gated workload is deployed into driftwood's cluster, so no posture claim has ever crossed a party boundary and the cross-org demand the owner described cannot be demonstrated.
findings.evidence: .estate-clone/platform/identity/spire/helmrelease.yaml:55 `trustDomain: acme.internal` and istio/helmrelease.yaml:56 (the only two trust-domain declarations in the estate clone). platform/identity/up.sh:13, platform/posture/up.sh:21, platform/access/up.sh:13, platform/eud/up.sh:8, platform/graded/up.sh:18 all default `CTX=kind-driftwood`. .estate-clone/tuppence/reset/up.sh:12 and verify-reach-secrets.sh:18 also default `CTX=kind-driftwood`; the live-proven SVID is `spiffe://acme.internal/posture/2.0.0/ns/tuppence-reset/sa/teller-current` — tuppence's namespace inside driftwood's cluster. grep for spire|spiffe across driftwood, ludlow, nist, ico returns nothing; only tuppence/reset matches, and only as manifests applied to driftwood. Three real KinD clusters exist and are Ready (scratchpad/live/talk-verify-live.json), so this is not a resource limit. Owner 2026-08-19: "2 split everything. We are demonstrating a multi org thing". Owner 2026-07-31 09:37 framed it cross-org: "the customer accounts reset service in a org might say it only supports the current version of the policy to talk to it". DECISION_AUDIT P180's now-recommendation: this is "the only mechanism that makes 'multi-org' mean something operationally rather than administratively".
findings.recommendation: Give each institution its own trust domain on its own cluster's SPIRE and federate them (bundle endpoint / federatesWith on the ClusterSPIFFEIDs). Move the tuppence flagship onto the tuppence cluster and make the reach gate admit a foreign trust domain's posture claim. That converts the layer from a per-cluster feature into the eco-system's cross-party attestation.
corrections: The owner never described a "cross-org posture demand." His 2026-07-31 example (customer accounts reset service requiring a caller's current policy version) is intra-org. His 2026-08-19 "split everything" mandate is about the estate's repo/org topology generally and was never tied by him to SPIFFE/SPIRE or identity. The single-trust-domain/single-cluster gap is real and worth fixing, but it should be presented as an architectural inference the reviewers drew (correctly attributed to DECISION_AUDIT's own recommendation), not as something the owner explicitly asked for.

findings.title: The identity substrate is the one population that runs uncaged
findings.claim: SPIRE, Istio, OpenBao, Pomerium and Dex run in namespaces carrying no `policy-as-versioned.dev/governed` label and their pods carry no policy-version claim, so they are matched by neither the orphan guard, nor cage-tier, nor the governed-namespace guard — the machinery that mints and checks every posture identity is itself outside the policy, against "nothing runs without a cage even if they're permissive".
findings.evidence: platform/identity/namespaces.yaml declares spire-system, istio-system, openbao with only `platform.acme.io/plane: identity`; platform/access/namespaces.yaml declares `access` with only `platform.acme.io/plane: access`. The only files carrying `policy-as-versioned.dev/governed` are the three adopters' gitops/apps/namespace.yaml and their composed guards. Both guards skip unclaimed pods by construction: render-orphan-guard.py:77 and render-governed-namespace-guard.py:69 gate on `object.metadata.?labels['...policy-version'].orValue('') != ''`; cage-tier.yaml matchConditions do the same. .scratch/govern-what-you-dont-control/issues/01-what-is-the-real-boundary.md:69-71: "it passes on £, while its actual pods (istiod, spire-server, openbao, pomerium, dex) are matched by no policy and admitted by default. Solving the hardest case first also proves the mechanism: if the shim can govern istiod, it can govern anything." All five issues in that effort are resolved/done; no wrap or shim exists anywhere in platform/.
findings.recommendation: Build the leading case that effort named: label the four identity/access namespaces governed, give the five charts a wrapped claim (a postRenderer stamping a platform-machinery version claim), and let cage-tier default them to a declared infra cage. Until istiod carries a cage, the claim that there is no uncaged state is false of exactly the components that make every other claim checkable.

findings.title: The cage tier label is forgeable; only the version label has a trust boundary
findings.claim: `posture.acme.io/tier` — the label deciding how hard a workload is caged — is read straight off the pod with no validating policy, no mutating clobber and no RBAC restriction, and both a missing and an unrecognised value fall through to `baseline`, the loosest tier, so any workload can self-select the weakest cage; the file's own comment asserts the opposite.
findings.evidence: platform/graded/policies/cage-tier.yaml:66-69 — `rawTier: object.metadata.?labels['posture.acme.io/tier'].orValue('baseline')`, then `tier: variables.rawTier in ['baseline','restricted','quarantine'] ? variables.rawTier : 'baseline'`. Its comment at lines 55-62 claims the tier is "never by the pod itself for a LOOSENING — a missing label or an unrecognized value both fall through to `baseline`, the loosest tier", the second clause contradicting the first. Nothing in the estate stamps the label at admission: grep matches only wargamer/tier_pr.py (which opens a PR editing it on the workload's own manifest), computed-semver corpus fixtures, and cage.py's own table. Compare posture-trust-boundary.yaml, which exists precisely because the version label needed a trust boundary. Owner 2026-08-22: "there is no real gate anymore. Just cages" — which makes the tier the only decision left, and it is the unprotected one.
findings.recommendation: Give the tier the treatment the version label already has: a ValidatingPolicy denying a tier the pod is not entitled to, a mutating clobber sourcing it from the priced decision, and default the absent case to the strictest tier rather than the loosest. The mechanism is already written next door.

findings.title: The SVID carries the version but not the cage — identity encodes the pre-evolution model
findings.claim: The posture SVID path is spiffe://<td>/posture/<version>/ns/<ns>/sa/<sa>, carrying only policy currency; there is no tier or cage segment anywhere, so a peer can demand "which version are you on" but not "what cage are you in" — the attribute the owner's model moved to between 2026-07-31 and 2026-08-22.
findings.evidence: platform/posture/spire/clusterspiffeid-posture.yaml:57 spiffeIDTemplate has one variable segment, the version. tuppence/reset/authorizationpolicy.yaml and openbao-role.yaml both glob on that version segment only. The cage tier and the `caged` label exist only as in-cluster pod labels stamped by cage-tier.yaml, invisible to any peer over mTLS. Owner 2026-07-31 09:37 asked for the policy to be "an attestation/property on the service account credentials"; by 2026-08-20 the policy IS the cage ("It's the spec of the cage that can change") and by 2026-08-22 "there is no real gate anymore. Just cages". The carrier was built to the July shape and never re-fitted.
findings.recommendation: Add the tier as a second leading segment (/posture/<version>/cage/<tier>/ns/...) so the existing single-prefix-wildcard trick still works, and let a counterparty's AuthorizationPolicy require both. A template change plus a glob change, not new machinery.
corrections: The version-only SPIFFE path is accurate and matches the owner's actual July-31 ask (version as the peer-attestable property); the "cage should also be in the identity" idea is the reviewer's own extrapolation from the later "always caged" enforcement-model language, not a real requirement the owner or the specs ever stated — cage tier is intentionally an in-cluster, per-org, admission-time enforcement output, not an identity attribute.

findings.title: The flagship reach/secret gate is pinned to posture/2.0.0 while the estate now ships 3.0.0
findings.claim: The posture bar is hardcoded as the literal string 2.0.0 in five files across two repositories with no derivation from and no verify cross-check against distribution/versions.yaml, which now declares 2.0.0, 2.0.1 and 3.0.0 — so a workload that upgrades to the current policy version gets SVID /posture/3.0.0/, matches neither glob, and is refused reach and its OpenBao secret exactly as if it were stale.
findings.evidence: .estate-clone/tuppence/reset/authorizationpolicy.yaml:41 `principals: ["acme.internal/posture/2.0.0/*"]`; openbao-role.yaml:51 `bound_claims='{"sub":"spiffe://acme.internal/posture/2.0.0/*"}'`; destinationrule.yaml:36; workloads.yaml:10; README.md:44. Against .estate-clone/platform/distribution/versions.yaml:31-33 declaring 2.0.0, 2.0.1 and 3.0.0, with real signed tags policy/v2.0.0, policy/v2.0.1, policy/v3.0.0 on the platform repo (HEAD 58ef9c5, "cs-27: signed release-gate evidence for policy/v3.0.0"). tuppence/reset/reach.py contains no reference to versions.yaml; its selfcheck only asserts the Istio glob and the OpenBao glob agree with each other, as authorizationpolicy.yaml's own comment states. Owner 2026-08-25: "goes in all the repos its supposed to go in".
findings.recommendation: Derive the bar from versions.yaml the way the orphan guard and shift-left already do (render-orphan-guard.py is the existing offline twin), and add the cross-check to verify-reach-secrets.sh so a version bump that does not reach the posture consumers is a build failure rather than a silent 403 on the newest workload.
corrections: none - claim confirmed as stated

findings.title: "Workload, device, commit and human all root to one attestation" is false for two of the four
findings.claim: The pitch-v6 narration asserts a single attestation root across four actor classes, but no device has ever attested (every tpm_devid selector is a placeholder string) and the human leg is a Dex static bcrypt account with no relationship to the Fulcio/Rekor workflow identity the estate actually verifies — three unrelated roots, not one.
findings.evidence: Narration line in .scratch/talk-spec/pitch-v6/narration.json: "Workload, device, commit and human all root to one attestation. Not one of them is trusted because of where it sits on a network." Against: platform/access/device/device-svid.yaml:23, platform/eud/vms/windows11-eud-device-svid.yaml:12, linux-eud-device-svid.yaml:11 and tpm-devid-enroll.sh's default all carry `tpm_devid:fingerprint:REPLACE_WITH_ATTESTED_TPM_FINGERPRINT`, with access/up.sh commenting "fingerprints still placeholders until attested". platform/access/oidc/dex-helmrelease.yaml:1-4 claims "one subject, two planes" but line 40 is `storage: type: memory` and lines 55-59 a single staticPasswords entry for operator@acme.internal with a bcrypt demo hash and no upstream connector. What the estate verifies as a signing identity is a workflow: platform/verify-certificate-identity-regexp.sh:21 expects `https://github.com/policy-as-versioned-platform/platform/.github/workflows/cut-release.yml@refs/heads/main`. platform/access/pomerium/helmrelease.yaml:75 `signingKey: ""` — the JWT assertion the apiserver would trust is unsigned.
findings.recommendation: Either narrate the true state (workload and commit root to attestations today; device and human are wired but have never attested, and here is what is missing) or close the smallest gap that makes the sentence true: a real EC signing key for Pomerium and Dex federated to the same GitHub OIDC the gitsign identity comes from. The owner's own 2026-07-31 rule covers this: build it, run it simulated, say on stage that it is simulated.
corrections: Two citation-level inaccuracies, neither undermining the substance: (1) the "fingerprints still placeholders until attested" comment lives in platform/eud/up.sh:22, not platform/access/up.sh (platform/access/up.sh has no such comment). (2) linux-eud-device-svid.yaml's placeholder selector is at line 12, not line 11 (line 11 is the `selectors:` key); windows11's citation at line 12 is correct as given.

findings.title: The EUD half was never built: no VM was ever booted, no vTPM ever ran
findings.claim: The owner's instruction was "build everything to demo with the vtpm and narrate in demo that its virtual but point carries", and the vTPM was never built: build-vm.sh creates empty qcow2 disks then prints the boot command for a human, the ISO paths are placeholder strings, and no VM, no swtpm and no tpm_devid attestation has ever run anywhere checkable.
findings.evidence: platform/eud/vms/*.json carry `iso: REPLACE_WITH_WINDOWS11_ISO_PATH` / `REPLACE_WITH_LINUX_ISO_PATH`; state/ holds ~196KB sparse qcow2 files and nothing else; README: build-vm.sh "never boots a VM or installs an OS ... GUI/ISO-gated and cannot run headless". .scratch/talk-spec/build/20-eud-vtpm-vms.md is marked PARTIAL with 1 of 3 ACs met and the audit note "nothing in the tree shows evidence one was ever built", "`ready-for-agent` was actively misleading". Owner 2026-07-31 10:38 and the standing rules "build everything" (2026-07-31), "nothing is a nice to have" (2026-07-23).
findings.recommendation: Either boot one Linux VM under UTM with swtpm, read the real EK fingerprint off the SPIRE server log and land one genuinely attested device SVID (the Linux side needs no ISO licence dance and proves the mechanism end to end), or tell the owner the EUD leg is cut and remove the claim from the map. Specs, templates and placeholders are the nice-to-have tier he banned.

findings.title: Neither graded human/device engine sits in an enforcement path
findings.claim: access.py and break-glass.py are pure CLIs invoked only by verify scripts; the only human/device decision actually enforced anywhere is Pomerium's route policy, a flat binary allow on one hardcoded email plus an approved-device flag — no op tiering, no step-up, no £, no cage.
findings.evidence: platform/access/pomerium/helmrelease.yaml:64-71 — `allow: and: [authenticated_user: true, email: {is: operator@acme.internal}, device: {is: approved}]`, the entire policy. platform/break-glass/README.md:107 states break-glass.py is meant to be "the forward-auth / external-authz decision a Pomerium route calls"; ESTATE_CODEMAP confirms "no such integration ... exists anywhere in the six directories read; it is purely a standalone CLI/library". verify-break-glass.sh has no live tail at all, by design. The layer the owner asked to be graded ("less a go/no-go decision, but more colour than that") is graded only where nothing calls it, and binary where something does.
findings.recommendation: Wire break-glass.py behind Pomerium's external-authz (a small HTTP shim over the existing decide() suffices) and delete the hardcoded email allow rule. Without that the human/device cage is a spreadsheet: it computes the right answer and nothing is obliged to obey it.
corrections: Cite platform/break-glass/README.md:34, not :107 (the file has only 96 lines); everything else quoted checks out against current repo state.

findings.title: Human/device assurance is not proportionate to the org, though the workload cage is
findings.claim: break-glass.py picks its assurance tier from a single global band table and reads the scenario's `org` field only to echo it, so the same £ operation demands the same factors in ludlow (£5k appetite) as in driftwood (£40k) — while the workload-side cage.py takes --org and reads appetite.json to do the opposite.
findings.evidence: platform/break-glass/assurance-bands.json is one flat object (step_up_at 10000, attest_at 100000, no_cage_at 1000000) with a note claiming calibration "against the estate's appetite ordering (ludlow strictest)" — a claim about how the constants were chosen, not a per-org lookup. In break-glass.py the only occurrence of `org` is line 96, `"org": scenario.get("org")`, inside the emitted record; nothing reads ../risk/appetite.json. Contrast platform/graded/README.md and cage.py: `--org ludlow` yields quarantine where `--org driftwood` yields baseline, reading platform/risk/appetite.json's per-org tolerances. Owner 2026-08-19: "the financial risk of 21707 doesn't seem sane to the same on every org, its proporiate to the org right?"
findings.recommendation: Scale the three band thresholds by the org's tolerance from appetite.json the way cage.py already does — a few lines, and it makes the human leg tell the same proportionality story as the workload leg instead of quietly undercutting it.

findings.title: The layer is not running today, and the failures are in the identity plane itself
findings.claim: On the review's own live probe (2026-08-27) the driftwood cluster shows spire-agent in CrashLoopBackOff with 398 restarts, the SPIRE OIDC discovery provider Unknown with 56 restarts, and six currency-controller Job pods in Error with an HTTP 404 from urllib — so no SVID can be minted or renewed and the post-admission re-evaluation has been failing every minute.
findings.evidence: scratchpad/live/talk-verify-live.json: before bring-up, driftwood non_running_pods = "6x currency-controller CronJob pods in Error; spire-spiffe-oidc-discovery-provider Unknown (56 restarts)"; after the one permitted talk/up.sh, "New red: spire-agent CrashLoopBackOff 398 restarts; currency-verify + currency-controller pods still Error (HTTP 404 from urllib in reconcile)"; up_sh_degraded_layers lists "platform: posture projection" and "platform: graded enforcement envelope (cages)". The 404 is consistent with currency.py's get_supported() (currency.py:147-157) reading a resourcesets/policy-versions object not present on that cluster — it carries a SUPPORTED_VERSIONS override "for demo paths where flux-operator isn't installed". The restart counts show these are not fresh failures from this probe. Owner 2026-08-25 on the last occurrence: "how on earth are you saying its working!?!!"
findings.recommendation: Fix the two red pods before the layer is claimed anywhere again, and make the currency controller's missing-ResourceSet path fail loudly at install rather than 404 silently once a minute. Then re-run verify-identity.sh --live and verify-posture-projection.sh and record the capture.

findings.title: The whole layer is effectively absent from the deliverable it was built for
findings.claim: The pitch-v6 narration — built 2026-08-25 under the instruction to cover "all of the features that we built ... the whole lot" — contains zero occurrences of SPIFFE, SPIRE, EUD or passkey, one each of posture and device, and the beats that do exercise this layer are listed as red; six build tickets and the owner's own 2026-07-31 pivot get roughly two sentences.
findings.evidence: Word counts over .scratch/talk-spec/pitch-v6/narration.json: SPIFFE 0, SPIRE 0, EUD 0, passkey 0, posture 1, device 1, identity 5 (mostly signing identities and org autonomy), attest 4. .scratch/talk-spec/pitch-v6/plan.md:119 lists "coexistence · graded · identity · posture · reach · access plane" in the red table with the reason "local. Three KinD clusters did not finish converging". Owner 2026-08-25: "Make sure that we're covering all of the features that we built in the work recently. the whole lot." Owner 2026-07-23: "nothing is a nice to have, you're either building it or your not".
findings.recommendation: Decide explicitly whether this layer is eco-system spine or a cut. If it is spine (H8-01's federation argument says it is), it needs a beat and a working cluster. If it is a cut, say so and stop maintaining six directories and six verify scripts for it. What it must not stay is built, red and unmentioned.

findings.title: Three encodings of the same human/device decision, none authoritative
findings.claim: The same question — may this human do this operation from this device — is answered by three independent artefacts with different rules: access.py's static OP_TIER table, break-glass.py's £-band table which its own note says replaces it, and Pomerium's YAML allow rule which enforces neither.
findings.evidence: platform/access/access.py:36-44 OP_TIER (read/list=1, write/exec=2, delete/break-glass/cluster-admin=3) over three cumulative factors. platform/break-glass/assurance-bands.json note: "This replaces access.py's static OP_TIER with the £-crossover it flagged as its upgrade path" — yet OP_TIER is still what verify-access.sh exercises and what platform/eud/verify-eud.sh re-uses for its WHfB assertion, and platform/access/README.md:88 still documents OP_TIER as live with the £ wiring as future work. platform/access/pomerium/helmrelease.yaml:64-71 is the third. Against the standing preference recorded in policy-composition and cited in ticket 19: "no second risk engine, no second appetite store".
findings.recommendation: Make break-glass.py the only decision function, have access.py expose the factor vocabulary and nothing else, point Pomerium at it, and delete OP_TIER — the same discipline break-glass.py already demonstrated by importing fair.py rather than reimplementing it.

findings.title: The secret half of posture-as-identity has never run
findings.claim: The OpenBao leg — the half answering the owner's original question "is this an openbao/istio/type thing?" — has never been exercised live: no `bao write auth/jwt/login` with a real JWT-SVID has ever run, and the OpenBao it would run against is a dev-mode instance with BAO_TOKEN=root on an unpinned openbao/openbao:latest image.
findings.evidence: .scratch/talk-spec/build/17-posture-gated-reach-secrets.md Status: "the reach half is now live-proven both ways; the secret (OpenBao) half is still only offline-proven both ways. Do not close until the secret half is independently live-proven too" and "no live `bao write auth/jwt/login` has actually run. This is the one remaining unmet criterion" — the stated cause is that teller-current/teller-stale run curlimages/curl with no spire-agent CLI in-pod to mint a JWT-SVID. .estate-clone/tuppence/reset/openbao-role.yaml:18 "Idempotent, dev-mode (root token)", :30-32 `image: openbao/openbao:latest`, `BAO_TOKEN: root`. platform/identity/openbao/helmrelease.yaml:31-34 dev mode, devRootToken: root, in-memory storage.
findings.recommendation: Swap the caller image for one carrying the spire-agent CLI (or mount the SPIFFE CSI socket with a small fetch-jwt sidecar) and run the login both ways. It is the cheapest remaining proof in the theme and it closes the one criterion the ticket itself refuses to close.
corrections: test

findings.title: Posture is delivered by kubectl, not by Flux, and is labelled so in its own script
findings.claim: platform/posture/up.sh is explicitly labelled "DEMO PATH, not delivery" and kubectl-applies the rendered posture policies and both ClusterSPIFFEIDs directly onto the cluster; no Kustomization or ResourceSet delivers the posture or identity layer, so the one layer carrying the versioned policy into a credential sits outside the versioned distribution mechanism.
findings.evidence: ESTATE_CODEMAP platform/posture how_it_runs: "NOT Flux-reconciled directly. up.sh is explicitly labelled 'DEMO PATH, not delivery' ... kubectl-applies only the rendered VERSIONED copies ... plus the unversioned posture ClusterSPIFFEID (not part of the versioned/renderer tree)". platform/identity how_it_runs: "ClusterSPIFFEID, PeerAuthentication, AuthorizationPolicy, Job ... are plain kubectl-applied manifests, not part of a Kustomization/ResourceSet tree for this ticket (14) — no distribution/ layer wraps identity itself." summary: This layer is the most technically real thing in the estate and the least connected to what the estate has since become. The engineering is genuine: SPIRE, Istio, OpenBao, Pomerium and Dex are real charts wired through Flux; the Kyverno mutate/validate trust boundary on the posture label is independently kyverno-test-proven; the posture-in-the-SVID-path trick is live-proven (a real pod held spiffe://acme.internal/posture/2.0.0/ns/tuppence-reset/sa/teller-current on 2026-08-20); the reach gate was proven both ways live; the currency controller and break-glass are honest, tested code that reuses fair.py rather than reimplementing it; and three real bugs were found by running it and fixed with regression asserts. Nothing here is cardboard. What has drifted is everything around it. It was designed on 2026-07-31 against a single fictitious organisation and never re-fitted after the 2026-08-19 "split everything": one trust domain called acme.internal, one cluster, tuppence's flagship workload deployed inside driftwood — so the one claim only this layer can make good, that a workload in one org can demand a posture attestation from a counterparty in another, has never been demonstrated and cannot be with what is built. It was designed before the cage evolution and still carries only the policy version in the SVID, not the cage tier — and the tier label that now decides everything has no trust boundary at all, so a workload can self-select the loosest cage while the version label it cannot forge is guarded twice. The substrate that mints every identity is itself the estate's only uncaged, unversioned population, which govern-what-you-dont-control named as its leading case, resolved on paper, and never built. The human and device legs are structurally complete and functionally inert: Pomerium's signing key is empty, no device has ever attested, no EUD VM was ever booted, and both graded decision engines are CLIs nothing calls, while the only enforced human rule is a hardcoded email. Today the cluster shows spire-agent crash-looping 398 times. And the deliverable the owner asked to cover "the whole lot" mentions SPIFFE zero times. On proportionality: the effort was not wasted, but it was spent on the wrong axis — depth on one cluster instead of breadth across parties. The eco-system north star needs one thing from this layer, and it is not more components: it needs a posture claim to cross a party boundary and be refused or admitted on its merits. Federating three trust domains, adding the cage tier to the SVID path, and guarding the tier label would buy that, and would cost less than any of the six tickets already built.

findings.title: Two disjoint Wardley engines exist, each missing exactly what the other has
findings.claim: twin/wardley.py and platform/wardley/wardley.py are independent implementations sharing no code and no data, and neither on its own is a Wardley engine: the twin has the value chain and the maths but no time and no money, the estate has time and money but no value chain and no maths.
findings.evidence: twin/wardley.py:83-96 implements D = vis(1-evo), K = (1-vis)evo, R, ported from arckit 6.7.5, and map_of() derives dependency risk per structural `needs` edge from the graph; it has no velocity, no horizon and no projection (`grep -rn velocity twin/*.py` returns nothing) and its docstring line 22 says no money enters. platform/wardley/wardley.py defines its own STAGES at line 68 (0.25/0.50/0.75/1.01), computes projection and the K-dial re-pricing, and emits £ through tcor; it contains no D/K/R, no anchor or user need, and no dependency edges — its rendered map/wardley-map.json body is `intel_version`, `horizon_years` and a flat `components` list. Neither file imports the other; `grep -rlI wardley` in the estate never leaves platform/wardley/, and nothing in twin/ references the estate map. Owner 2026-08-04: "our wardley engine can do this on scale for an ever increasing number of factors".
findings.recommendation: Under the loosely-coupled eco-system north star, do not merge the code — make one of them the publisher and the other the consumer. The twin holds the value chain and the judgement skills; it should publish a signed, versioned map artefact (positions, dependencies, movement) that the estate's forward layer consumes as its intel feed, replacing hand-typed market-intel.json coordinates. That is also exactly the feed a Gartner-shaped party would sell.
corrections: One cited piece of evidence could not be verified: the "Owner 2026-08-04" quote ("our wardley engine can do this on scale for an ever increasing number of factors") does not appear anywhere in the repo, .estate-clone, or the supplied OWNER_BRIEF.md context file — no transcript or note contains it. It may come from an out-of-band conversation not persisted anywhere I can check, so I can't confirm or disprove it, but as written it is unsourced. This doesn't affect the core technical claim (two disjoint, structurally incomplete Wardley implementations), which is fully and precisely confirmed by the code.

Owner 2026-07-23: "We should leverage Wardley mapping into this too as a means to track commodification and understanding the chains"; owner 2026-08-05: "the large point of wardley mapping is to have a thing you can argue with and debate" — a scatter with no chain gives an audience nothing structural to argue with.

duplications_and_contradictions: Two Wardley implementations with no shared code and disjoint capabilities: twin/wardley.py (arckit-ported D/K/R, value-chain dependency risk, no time, no money, action bands deliberately excluded) and platform/wardley/wardley.py (its own STAGES bands at line 68, forward projection, ATTACK_COST_COLLAPSE_K, £ via tcor, no D/K/R, no chain). Neither imports the other; nothing in twin/ reads the estate map and nothing in the estate reads the twin's.

arckit is credited as the source of the twin's Wardley maths and pinned at 6.7.5 in the port comment; the installed plugin cache now holds 6.8.0 through 6.12.0 and nothing invokes any /arckit:wardley skill at runtime, in either tree. The owner's 2026-08-04 framing ('the wardley skill we have available can do this and we can wire up with claude code to refresh that') is therefore true only of a one-time copy of constants.

'AI-Wardley' as a name versus zero AI in the layer: wardley.py:2 docstring, the note string at :243, `author: "ai-generated"` at :190 and :207, talk-spec/spec.md:144/241/277, talk-spec/map.md:43, the-whole-model.md:54/134/198, talk/deck.md:173, talk/verify-all.sh:44 and pitch-v6/deck.html:648 all carry the label; the cluster contains no model call and no network access.

market-intel.json's pqc-transport-migration note declares the defensive-credit path impossible ('finding F2'), while wardley.py:233-236 and the live forward-signal output both exercise it — a contradiction inside signed data that cannot be corrected because the signing key is absent.

wardley/README.md and five docstrings in wardley.py say 'all three institutions (driftwood, tuppence, ludlow)'; institutions() reads risk/appetite.json, which carries four orgs, so the live run prints '11 forward drift(s) across 4 institution(s)' with `platform` scoring itself against its own root-of-trust band.

Build ticket 23 was re-statused to done by audit mo-02 on evidence that includes a gitsign claim for a script that neither performs gitsign nor can run; the same tree's HONESTY-niobium-beat.md and multi-org-estate ticket 06 comment are, by contrast, unusually candid about their own limits — honesty is applied unevenly between the research documents and the ticket closures.

Story 41 ('sweeping for Wardley-play preconditions on schedule') and story 42 (the sweep as the counterweight to negativity bias) are both marked delivered by build ticket 46, but twin/schedule.py's own docstring states the clock was never built and no scheduled workflow exists anywhere — so the counterweight to the negativity bias, which only works if it runs unprompted, has never run unprompted.

The prediction-market question the owner asked directly on 2026-08-19 ('did we get polymarket integration in to the risk modelling?') was closed by multi-org-estate ticket 13 with 'nothing to build here' in the estate; twin/market_signals.py exists but reaches no venue and is called by nothing outside its own tests and one invariant check. DECISION_AUDIT P031 already grades this 'narrowed'.
summary: The Wardley work is real, careful, well-tested arithmetic that is wired to nothing. Both engines exist and both run green: the estate's forward layer genuinely projects commoditisation, genuinely re-prices attacker frequency through a documented K dial, genuinely gates defensive credit on corroborated enactment, and genuinely proves tamper rejection offline; the twin genuinely ports arckit's D/K/R and derives a map from its graph with no separate authoring step. But across the entire six-org estate the string "wardley" appears only inside platform/wardley/, and in the twin neither pricing.py nor enact.py references it at all — so no Wardley output has ever moved a cage, a price or a policy anywhere a person could observe it. The three things the owner asked for by name are each missing in a specific way. Anticipation at scale: nothing is scheduled anywhere in any repo, and the map cannot even be re-signed because the private key exists in no checkout, so the factor set is frozen at nine hand-typed components. AI: there is no model call in the layer that is called AI-Wardley in nine files and stamps its output "ai-generated"; the one component that would earn the name, a headline-to-coordinate classifier, was correctly identified in writing and then filed under "not yet specified" behind an assistant-chosen precondition, after the owner had explicitly offered to have it built. The niobium headline: it is committed, but as the map's deliberate non-firing control, and the quantum component beside it is projected to 0.45 and never crosses a boundary, so the played-forward consequence chain exists only in a pitch-v4 research file run against an uncommitted /tmp intel variant, and is absent from pitch-v6 entirely. Underneath all of that sits a structural split the north star can actually fix: the twin holds the value chain and the judgement, the estate holds the movement and the money, and neither knows the other exists. The eco-system framing gives them the missing relationship — an independent intel publisher (which does not exist; the feeds org 404s and market-intel.json is published_by the same party that reads it) selling a signed commoditisation feed that the estate's forward layer consumes as a pinned dependency. That one rewiring would answer H5-01, H5-06, H5-10 and most of H5-11 together, and is the smallest change that turns this theme from a demo command into the anticipatory, subscribable layer the owner described on 2026-08-19. We are demonstrating a multi org thing" (2026-08-19); the twin as the intelligence — "We're effectively creating a digital twin of the organisation and giving gameplay opportunities To answer the what if fast forward rewind Play" (2026-08-04); cages as enforcement — "you're always caged even if it's a permissive one. It's the spec of the cage that can change" (2026-08-20), "3 there is no real gate anymore. Just cages" (2026-08-22), "there must never be an exemption ledger EVER" (2026-08-20); one £ currency — "one £ risk currency" so "a pay rise (HR control) and security hardening (tech control) become comparable" (2026-08-04) and org-proportionate — "the financial risk of 21707 doesn't seem sane to the same on every org, its proporiate to the org right?" (2026-08-19); provenance — "All of which makes commits and PRs with their own attest-able identity that demonstrate provenance" (2026-07-23). Standing constraints across all of it: "nothing is a nice to have, you're either building it or your not" (2026-07-23), "all of this is 'the policy'" (2026-07-31), "flux is a integral part/enabler to this (unless we prove otherwise)" (2026-08-05), "You've got nothing about Monte Carlo modelling and continuous refreshing of things" (2026-08-19).
what_was_specified: Nine documents each specify a PART, none specifies the whole. (1) `docs/PRD.md` + `README.md` + `CONTEXT.md` still open on the Phase-0 framing — "a faithful re-implementation of Chris Nesbitt-Smith's Policy as [Versioned] Code thesis onto Flux CD" — unrevised since July. (2) `docs/north-star-modern-reference.md` is the only file in the repo with "north star" in its name; last touched 2026-07-14; its subject is an OCI/cosign transport upgrade to the faithful floor. (3) `.scratch/talk-spec/the-whole-model.md` (2026-07-31) is the only whole-system picture; its hourglass still draws an EXEMPTIONS LEDGER node and mentions the twin zero times. (4) `.scratch/twin/map.md` (last commit 2026-08-18) and `.scratch/twin/spec.md` (2026-08-11) make the twin the destination and demote governance to "one enactment arm, not the point", call the estate "a prior to test, not a foundation", declare the talk "a byproduct", and instruct "Bin the `estate/` monorepo + the KinD clusters". (5) `.scratch/multi-org-estate/map.md` (2026-08-19) charts the six real orgs and explicitly fences the twin out: "Reusing twin machinery is in scope; extending the twin is not." (6) `.scratch/policy-composition/map.md` (2026-08-21) comes closest to the eco-system — "A regulator publishes controls; a publisher ships implementations; an adopter inherits both and adds its own. Pricing and threat parents contribute no rules but move the £" — but its own scope line confines it to "the composition step on the adopter side". (7) `docs/ARCHIVE.md` (2026-08-21) declares the hub superseded and research-only. (8) `.estate-clone/platform/party/schema.json` encodes roles publisher/risk-bearer/adopter and parent kinds controls/implementations/pricing/threat — the eco-system's actual grammar, in a JSON Schema, with no prose document that reads it as a system. (9) `.scratch/talk-spec/pitch-v6/plan.md` (2026-08-25, untracked in git) is the only artefact naming both, and it names them as "both north stars" — plural.
what_was_built: Two large, well-built, near-disjoint systems. ESTATE: six real public GitHub organisations (`policy-as-versioned-{platform,driftwood,tuppence,ludlow,nist,ico}`, confirmed live via `gh api /user/orgs`), a signed party artefact per adopter declaring roles and pinned parents, cross-party composition with six structural refusals, a computed-semver release gate, a FAIR Monte Carlo engine (10k iterations, ALE/VaR95/TVaR/TCoR) with per-org appetite bands (driftwood 40000, tuppence 15000, ludlow 5000, platform 10000), a three-rung cage ladder with priced dials, Bühlmann calibration, five signed versioned feeds, a Wardley forward layer, and a war-gamer with exactly one real PR-opening path (`platform/wargamer/tier_pr.py`). TWIN: 33,314 lines of Python in `twin/` — typed graph, PERT/Monte Carlo pricing, Bühlmann–Straub credibility, proper scoring rules, forecast book, causal accounts, Wardley port, synthetic substrate, propose-only enactment, ethics gate, 73/73 computed capability depth. NEITHER READS THE OTHER. The estate imports nothing from `twin/` (the only `twin` tokens in estate code are `orphan_twin`/`governed_twin` — an unrelated homonym meaning "offline twin of a live check"). `twin/` reads the estate only in three narrow places (`enact.py` reads committed GitRepository pins out of `.estate-clone/`, `drift.py` reads a driftwood sample log, `verdict.py` reads a driftwood protocol file) and cites three `estate/…` paths that no longer exist after the mo-12 split. No network read occurs anywhere in either feeds cluster or the twin ("REAL FEED READING: none"). No `policy-as-versioned-feeds` org and no `policy-as-versioned-twin` org exist; the twin has no repo, no org, and no `party.yaml`, so it is not a participant in the eco-system it is supposed to be the intelligence of.

findings.title: The orgs are not the twin's example consumers — the two centres model two disjoint casts
findings.claim: The twin models seven real-world companies and zero of the estate's three institutions, so "the orgs as an example consumers to demonstrate the whole eco-system operating" cannot be demonstrated by running the system as built.
findings.evidence: Occurrence counts in /Users/cns/httpdocs/controlplane/policy-as-versioned-flux/twin/fixtures.py: netflix 152, intel 104, carillion 88, enron 46, kodak 33, maersk 29, royal_mail 26+19+6 — and driftwood 0, tuppence 0, ludlow 0. The twin's demo beat scripts are twin/beat-intel.sh, twin/beat-netflix.sh, twin/beat-royal-mail.sh. The estate's risk store, .estate-clone/platform/risk/appetite.json, carries driftwood/tuppence/ludlow/platform and no twin subject. The only cross-references anywhere are three narrow file reads in twin/enact.py, twin/drift.py and twin/verdict.py against `.estate-clone/driftwood/`.

findings.title: Two contradictory enforcement ladders, on the owner's own central mechanism
findings.claim: The twin's enforcement ladder forbids per-rung risk-reduction numbers as unfalsifiable, and the estate's cage ladder is built entirely out of per-rung risk-reduction numbers — so the two halves disagree in code about how a cage works.
findings.evidence: /Users/cns/httpdocs/controlplane/policy-as-versioned-flux/twin/enforcement-grades.yaml lines 10-15: "**No rung carries a number, and the loader refuses one.** … A reduction per rung would be a free multiplier: tighten the rung, earn more credit, with nothing evidencing it. That is exactly the unfalsifiable claim build ticket 30's grade exists to stop, so the ladder orders consequence and prices nothing." Against /Users/cns/httpdocs/controlplane/policy-as-versioned-flux/.estate-clone/platform/graded/cage.py:65-84 — `TIERS = {"baseline": {"reduce": 0.30, "cost": 500, …}, "restricted": {"reduce": 0.70, "cost": 2000, …}, "quarantine": {"reduce": 0.92, "cost": 6000, …}}` — with cage.py:96-114 `caged_residual`/`tcor` multiplying by exactly that `reduce`. The owner's evolution ran the estate's way: "you're always caged even if it's a permissive one. It's the spec of the cage that can change" (2026-08-20), "there is no real gate anymore. Just cages. That may ultimately degrade to something that is too expensive to run or not functional" (2026-08-22) — degradation by expense requires the per-rung price the twin's ladder refuses.
findings.recommendation: Settle it in the north-star document, in the owner's direction: cages carry a price, because "too expensive to run" is his stated bottom rung. Then reconcile — the twin's objection is a real one (an unevidenced reduction multiplier is a free lunch), so the answer is that the reduction stays but must carry an evidence grade, which is exactly the machinery twin/credibility.py and the estate's honesty/calibration.py both already have. One ladder, priced, evidence-graded, in one place.
corrections: none

Narrow the "degradation by expense requires the per-rung price the twin's ladder refuses" claim: the owner's "too expensive to run" quote is satisfied by a per-tier *cost* number, which twin's ladder already permits (line 55) — only the per-tier *reduction/mitigation* fraction is the disputed, refused number. The two-implementation contradiction over the `reduce` field itself still stands.

Two meanings of "twin" in one codebase: the digital twin (twin/), and "offline twin" — the offline render of a live check — used throughout computed-semver and policy-composition (orphan_twin, governed_twin, 17-demo-scripts-as-offline-twins.md). Grepping the estate for the digital twin returns almost only the homonym.

twin/map.md:57-58 "Bin the `estate/` monorepo + the KinD clusters" versus live KinD cluster configs in .estate-clone/{driftwood,tuppence,ludlow}/kind/ and three live-reconcile beats in the honesty gate.
twin/map.md:35 and spec.md:412 "the talk is a byproduct, never its driver" versus pitch-v6 built 2026-08-25 as the session's deliverable, and the owner's own "this is a demo of it all" (2026-08-19).

.scratch/talk-spec/the-whole-model.md:82 EXEMPTIONS LEDGER node versus CONTEXT.md:53 "A banned concept. There are none, ever."

docs/PRD.md / README.md / CONTEXT.md opening framing ("a faithful re-implementation of Policy as [Versioned] Code onto Flux CD") versus every ambition stated from 2026-07-23 onward; and docs/north-star-modern-reference.md holding the name "north star" while describing a July transport upgrade.

The eco-system's regulator-publishes-consequence edge exists in the schema and not in the pins.
multi-org-estate/map.md fences the twin out ("extending the twin is not [in scope]") while pitch-v6 presents the twin as half the deliverable — the same week.
summary: The north star is an eco-system; the project is two systems that do not read each other. Both are real and substantial — six live GitHub orgs with signed cross-party composition, a computed release gate, priced cages and a FAIR engine on one side; 33,314 lines of forecast-scoring, causal and Wardley machinery on the other — and there is no document anywhere that says they are one thing. The word "eco-system" appears nowhere in the corpus in the owner's sense; the closest statement is policy-composition's party model, which its own spec bounds to the composition step. The demotion that caused the split is still on the page: twin/map.md (last edited 2026-08-18) and twin/spec.md (2026-08-11) declare governance "one enactment arm, not the point", the estate "a prior to test", the talk "a byproduct", and the KinD clusters "binned" — and every one of those was reversed in practice across Aug 19-25 without either document being touched. The evidence that they are two systems rather than one is structural, not editorial: the twin models seven real firms and zero of the estate's three institutions; the estate imports nothing from twin/ (its only "twin" tokens are an unrelated homonym); the single proposed seam between them was resolved as "no estate work"; the twin has no GitHub org, no repo and no party.yaml, so it is not a participant in the eco-system it is supposed to be the intelligence of; and the two halves now disagree in code about how a cage works, on the one mechanism the owner's own thinking evolved toward. Around that sit three stale framings that make the drift hard to see from inside: docs/ARCHIVE.md calls the hub research-only while eight ADRs landed there after, docs/north-star-modern-reference.md holds the name "north star" while describing a July transport upgrade, and the-whole-model.md — the only whole-system picture — still draws an exemptions ledger the owner banned. The fix is not more building. It is one dated north-star document that names the parties, the seams and the currency; a promotion of the party grammar that already exists in platform/party/schema.json into that document; making driftwood, tuppence and ludlow the twin's subjects so one cast tells one story; and superseding, with dates rather than deletions, the four documents that still describe a different destination.

theme: H2 — cages and graded enforcement versus binary admission
owner_ambition: The owner's model moved in three recorded steps and he named that movement today as the one thing in the record he stands behind. 2026-07-31: "we should think about other things the policy should leverage and control, its not necessarily just around admission or you can run or not... you could allow a degraded or resource constrained state. so if a running application falls behind on patching it could still potentially run, but with contrained iops, cpu, memory, network etc, or maybe have more waf rules applied to it (so more expensive to run) because its less trusted... so its less a go/no-go decision, but more colour than that while still carrying the levels of proportionality". 2026-07-31: "this is all just 'the policy'... we're not carving exemptions, or greater complexity". 2026-08-20 07:43: "3 the pod stopping is just the implementation of the incoming policy because it does not fit in an available cage". 2026-08-20 07:46: "5 you're always caged even if it's a permissive one. It's the spec of the cage that can change". 2026-08-20 08:32: "2 it runs in a cage that simulates it, nothing runs without a cage even if they're permissive". 2026-08-20 08:42: "there must never be an exemption ledger EVER, this is a banned concept explicitly, everything is codified". 2026-08-21 16:20: "its never an exemption it'll be a informed caging based on risk appetite/threat intel". 2026-08-22 10:23: "3 there is no real gate anymore. Just cages. That may ultimately degrade to something that is too expensive to run or not functional". 2026-08-27: "my thoughts through grilling sessions did evolve though from binary admission to cage/constraint shape and around risk assessment was done and what we modelled". Read together: one enforcement instrument, the cage; every workload inside one at all times; the cage spec the only variable; the £ (appetite and threat intel) picks the spec; refusal is not a separate instrument but the bottom rung, reached when the price leaves no satisfiable spec.
what_was_specified: .scratch/computed-semver/spec.md is the only document that carries the owner's model correctly, and it carries it exactly: "There is no separate refused verdict class. Refusal is the bottom rung of the cage ladder"; "Every workload is always caged, and the cage spec is what changes. The engine therefore compares cage specs, not verdict enums. There is no uncaged state. deny is the degenerate case where no satisfiable spec exists" (lines 210-214). Nothing else does. CONTEXT.md, the repo's domain authority, still teaches the opposite as doctrine: a "Lane-keeping vs. gate" section defining Gate as "a locked door... A hard admission block", ruling "The system must support BOTH. A gate-only system is the exact mistake the mea-culpa walked back", with "Audit = lane-keeping; Deny = gate" as the engine mapping (CONTEXT.md:71-81); semver anchored on "any change that can turn a pass into a fail at the gate" and "Compliant means admitted" (CONTEXT.md:118-124); "Orphan guard — A deterministic catch-all ValidatingPolicy that denies at admission" (CONTEXT.md:195). The canonical model diagram .scratch/talk-spec/the-whole-model.md:70-77 still draws "the neck — one admission decision" containing "ENFORCEMENT / ADMISSION — Audit = observe · Deny = block", and at line 82 an "EXEMPTIONS LEDGER (the conditional branches) — each: priced · scoped · expiring · versioned" node: the concept banned by name, carrying a clock ADR-0006 also bans. platform/graded/README.md specifies three tiers and a Deny bottom rung but scopes the cage to workloads that claim a policy version, stating "A pod claiming no policy version at all (system/COTS) is out of scope, unmatched. Never denies." ADR-0014 specifies the sibling hole-closer as a ValidatingPolicy that "denies an unclaimed pod inside a governed namespace". twin/enforcement-grades.yaml specifies a different, four-rung ladder (observe/warn/constrain/block) and specifies that it must never be priced. Of the 26 audited provisional decisions on this theme, 11 are marked superseded-by-owner and 5 drifted; six are recommended for reversal or re-grilling by the audit itself (P001, P028, P128, P129, P132, P134, P143).
what_was_built: Real and faithful: platform/computed-semver/cage_engine.py Track 2 compares rendered cage specs on a permissiveness partial order across cpu/mem/priorityClass/dropAll/readOnlyRootFs/waf, and models "there is no uncaged state" as UNCAGED at the top of the lattice so cage-tier-newly-added falls out as a narrowing with no special case. platform/graded/cage.py is a genuine priced ladder (TIERS carries reduce and cost per tier; select_tier walks loosest-to-tightest against the org's appetite band; tcor() books residual + cost-of-controls; oscal_risk() refuses to emit for a Deny because nothing is retained). platform/break-glass/break-glass.py is the most graded thing in the estate: a £-crossover over assurance-bands.json with a real CAGE rung between STEP_UP and DENY. platform/tcor/tcor.py competes cage against fix, deny and transfer on price. The cage-tier MutatingPolicy does default a cage: an in-currency pod with no tier label, or an unrecognised value, falls through to baseline rather than to a skip. Built and inert: cages[] is empty in driftwood, ludlow and tuppence composed/evidence.json — the only code path that fills it (apply_restatements, a weaker overlay.restate entry) cannot fire because all three party.yaml files carry "restate: []". No adopter workload manifest anywhere carries posture.acme.io/tier; the only files that do are generated corpus fixtures. prices[] shows five of six priced parent positions standing at tier "deny" right now (ludlow and tuppence on both parents, driftwood on ico), every one changed:false and proposed_as:"issue" — the £ has already reached the bottom rung estate-wide and nothing acts on it. Live: talk/verify-all.sh --live fails the beat named "graded response: caged by degree, not denied" with "FAIL: cage-tier-2-0-1 MutatingPolicy not installed live"; up.sh reports "platform: graded enforcement envelope (cages) degraded"; driftwood's cluster is still reconciled to v1.0.0 and its currency-controller CronJob pods are in Error (HTTP 404), so no tier is ever stamped post-admission. Still binary and shipped: composed/orphan-guard.yaml carries validationActions [Deny] in all three orgs; platform/risk/appetite.json states in its own note "Enforcement is binary here (Audit vs Deny)"; platform/compose/composition.py:230 defines the cross-party strictness ladder as STRICTNESS = {"Audit": 0, "Deny": 1}; composition carries eleven refusal branches including one refusing an adopter for widening its own baseline; composed/governed-namespace-guard.yaml ships as Audit though ADR-0014 says it denies; platform/access/access.py's DENY/STEP_UP/ALLOW gate is still shipped and selfchecked alongside break-glass.py; twin/enforcement.py enforces a GRADE_NEVER_PRICES invariant whose loader fails validation if any rung carries a number.

findings.title: No workload in the estate has ever been caged by degree
findings.claim: Across all three adopter organisations, cages[] is empty, no workload manifest carries a cage tier, no priced tier has ever changed, and the live beat named 'graded response: caged by degree, not denied' fails — so the graded cage has never once acted on a real workload.
findings.evidence: driftwood/composed/evidence.json, ludlow/composed/evidence.json, tuppence/composed/evidence.json all show "cages": [] and every prices[] entry with "changed": false. platform/compose/composition.py:665-741 (apply_restatements) is the sole producer of a cages[] entry and only fires on an overlay.restate entry weaker than the inherited action; driftwood/party.yaml, ludlow/party.yaml and tuppence/party.yaml all carry 'overlay: {add: [], restate: []}'. grep for posture.acme.io/tier across the whole estate clone returns only platform/computed-semver/generated-corpus/spine/*.yaml fixtures and the proposer's own test assertions — driftwood/deploy/pod.yaml, the one real workload, carries only policy-as-versioned.dev/policy-version: "2.0.0". Live probe scratchpad/live/talk-verify-live/verify-all-live-after-up.txt:19-20 'graded response: caged by degree, not denied  FAIL (exit) / last: FAIL: cage-tier-2-0-1 MutatingPolicy not installed live'; up-driftwood.txt:156 'platform: graded enforcement envelope (cages) degraded'. Owner 2026-08-20: 'nothing runs without a cage even if they're permissive'.
findings.recommendation: Before anything else on this theme, make one workload really move between tiers end to end: fix the currency-controller's HTTP 404, install cage-tier at the released version on driftwood, and drive one pod baseline -> restricted with the £ that chose it. Until that runs, every cage claim in the deck is a claim about code that has never touched a workload.
corrections: none

findings.title: The unversioned population runs uncaged, and the estate documents that as intentional
findings.claim: cage-tier's matchConditions require a non-empty policy-version label, so every pod that claims nothing — kube-system, Flux, Kyverno, SPIRE, Istio, OpenBao, Pomerium, Dex, git-server and every COTS workload — is unmatched and uncaged, and platform/graded/README.md states this as the design.
findings.evidence: platform/graded/policies/cage-tier.yaml:59-63, matchConditions 'claims-a-policy-version': object.metadata.?labels['policy-as-versioned.dev/policy-version'].orValue('') != ''. platform/graded/README.md: 'A pod claiming no policy version at all (system/COTS) is out of scope, unmatched. Never denies.' and 'A pod that claims no policy version at all is a different population, and this ticket does not touch it.' composed/orphan-guard.yaml carries the same matchCondition has-policy-version-label, so the catch-all only catches pods that already opted in. Owner 2026-08-20: 'nothing runs without a cage even if they're permissive' and 'it runs in a cage that simulates it'. DECISION_AUDIT P174, verdict re-grill: 'the rebuild reintroduced the bypass under a new name, and the current codebase documents the hole as intentional'.
findings.recommendation: Put the owner's absolute to him as the scoping question it actually is, then default the cage rather than classify its absence: a MutatingPolicy assigning the strictest cage to any pod that claims nothing, with infrastructure claiming an explicit infra cage. That deletes the three-way taxonomy (P129/P132) rather than adding to it.
corrections: The matchConditions/scope gap itself is real and verified (uncaged unversioned population exists in the code). But the finding overstates it as settled/intentional design when the actual README language explicitly leaves it open and unresolved, and the cited 'DECISION_AUDIT P174' verdict does not exist in the repo — that citation should be dropped or replaced with the real, findable source (the govern-what-you-dont-control ticket 03 grilling doc, 2026-08-20), which shows the gap already flagged for closure rather than defended as intentional.

One nuance worth flagging (doesn't change the verdict): the finding's phrase "the estate documents that as intentional" overstates the README slightly — the doc's own words are that this scoping is explicitly *not* a closed decision ("a real question, genuinely left open... not a decision this policy body has already made," spun out to ticket 02 answer #5). So the codebase documents the gap as a known-open question, not a settled design choice — but the gap itself, and its contradiction of the owner's absolute, is real and correctly identified.

If reported, downgrade from "critical drift/contradiction" to a known-boundary note: the unversioned/COTS population is deliberately out of scope for cage-tier.yaml per an explicit owner decision (ticket 02 answer #5), already implemented, tested, and documented — not an oversight or an unacknowledged gap. Any follow-up should be framed as reopening a settled scope decision, not as newly-discovered drift.

findings.title: The £ has already reached the bottom rung across the estate and nothing enacts it
findings.claim: Five of the six priced parent positions in the shipped composed artefacts stand at tier 'deny' today, every one marked changed:false and proposed_as:'issue', so 'deny is the bottom rung reached by the £' resolves in practice to filing a GitHub issue while the workloads keep running in the loosest cage.
findings.evidence: driftwood/composed/evidence.json prices[]: ico pricing old_tier/proposed_tier 'deny', price £16,901,471, proposed_as 'issue'. ludlow and tuppence: BOTH parents (ico pricing and platform threat) at 'deny', proposed_as 'issue'. platform/compose/composition.py:955-960 and :1017 — DENY_TIER is marked as an issue subject because 'the cage-tier MutatingPolicy coerces any OTHER label value to "baseline" -- so a merged tier: deny label would invert the proposal in silence (ADR-0015)'. platform/wargamer/tier_pr.py:157-180 opens a GitHub issue for that case. platform/graded/policies/cage-tier.yaml:66-69: variables.rawTier in ['baseline','restricted','quarantine'] ? variables.rawTier : 'baseline' — the tightest verdict the engine can produce coerces to the loosest cage it can apply. Owner 2026-08-22: 'there is no real gate anymore. Just cages. That may ultimately degrade to something that is too expensive to run or not functional.'
findings.recommendation: Give the ladder its bottom rung — a fourth tier below quarantine that is the 'too expensive to run or not functional' state — so the price never leaves the cage vocabulary and the proposer always has a tier to write. Fix the coercion in the same edit: an unknown tier must fail closed to the strictest tier, not open to baseline. This is DECISION_AUDIT P143, verdict reverse, and it is a live safety inversion, not a wording point.

findings.title: The estate's own risk store and its newest composition engine both declare enforcement binary
findings.claim: platform/risk/appetite.json — the single appetite store the cage engine itself reads — states in its own note that 'Enforcement is binary here (Audit vs Deny)', and platform/compose/composition.py encodes the cross-party strictness ladder as a two-value enum, so the newest work in the estate judges every restatement on the binary the owner abolished.
findings.evidence: platform/risk/appetite.json note: 'Enforcement is binary here (Audit vs Deny): a control's residual risk-bought (ALE_warn - ALE_deny) above the org's tolerance MUST escalate Audit->Deny'. platform/graded/cage.py:52-54 imports that same enforce/appetite pair ('Reuses ../fair/fair.py and ../risk/enforce.py... No new risk engine, no new appetite store'). platform/compose/composition.py:230: STRICTNESS = {"Audit": 0, "Deny": 1}, used at :692 as the accept/cage test for every cross-party restatement. Kyverno's ValidatingPolicy supports a Warn action; grep for 'Warn' across the estate clone returns nothing. Owner 2026-08-20/22: 'you're always caged even if it's a permissive one. It's the spec of the cage that can change' / 'there is no real gate anymore. Just cages.'
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the appetite.json note in cage-spec terms and replace the two-value STRICTNESS enum with the permissiveness partial order cage_engine.py already implements. Composition is the piece the eco-system story rests on; it should compare cage specs like the release gate does, not verdict letters.
corrections: The binary STRICTNESS ladder in composition.py and the "binary here" note in appetite.json are intentional, ADR-0016-documented consequences of Kyverno's ValidatingPolicy schema having only Audit/Deny — not a stale contradiction of the owner's graded-cage vision. The permissiveness partial order the finding asks composition.py to adopt already exists and is already used, in cage_engine.py's Track 2 (release gate) and cage.py (pricing), which composition.py itself calls for the graded case rather than re-implementing.

findings.title: The proportionality money shot is binary, and it is a hub fixture that reaches no organisation
findings.claim: The headline demo beat 'same control, same £, Audit in driftwood, Deny in ludlow' is rendered from two files in the hub's verify/ tree for a control that is not distributed to any org, while the policies actually shipped to driftwood, tuppence and ludlow are byte-identical, so the estate demonstrates no enforcement proportionality at all.
findings.evidence: verify/proportionality/render.py renders verify/proportionality/policies/encrypt-at-rest-driftwood.yaml and encrypt-at-rest-ludlow.yaml only; grep for 'encrypt-at-rest' across the entire .estate-clone (all six org repos) returns zero hits. In the shipped artefacts, driftwood/composed/policies/v3.0.0/require-nonroot.yaml, tuppence's and ludlow's are all Audit; posture-trust-boundary is Deny in all three; driftwood and ludlow cage-tier.yaml at v3.0.0 diff clean apart from the composed-for label. pitch-v6 narration segment 15 is captured from .scratch/talk-spec/pitch-v6/captures/proportionality.txt, whose live step reports 'live(ludlow): cluster reachable but Kyverno CRDs not installed — skipping dry-run (offline proof stands)'. And re-cut the beat as a cage-spec divergence rather than an Audit/Deny flip, which is the version of it the owner would now recognise.

findings.title: Four enforcement ladders exist and they disagree on whether a rung has a price
findings.claim: The system carries four independent enforcement ladders — cage.py's three priced tiers, risk/enforce.py's binary Audit/Deny, twin/enforcement-grades.yaml's four unpriced rungs, and access.py's static three-tier gate superseded but not retired by break-glass.py's priced four-rung one — and no document reconciles them.
findings.evidence: platform/graded/cage.py:65-84 TIERS with per-tier reduce and cost. platform/risk/enforce.py:53 verdict = 'Deny' if risk_bought > tolerance else 'Audit'. twin/enforcement-grades.yaml grades observe/warn/constrain/block with the header 'No rung carries a number, and the loader refuses one'. platform/access/access.py:36-51 OP_TIER static table with DENY/STEP_UP/ALLOW, still shipped, still run by up.sh ('decision engine selfcheck (the graded human/device gate)', scratchpad/live/talk-verify-live/up-driftwood.txt:181) alongside platform/break-glass/break-glass.py:57 which adds 'CAGE  # a retained but read-only/scoped session — the graded rung access.py lacks' and prices the bar from assurance-bands.json. The policy-composition effort's own standing preference was 'no second risk engine, no second appetite store'.
findings.recommendation: Name one ladder and make the others projections of it. The owner's model gives the answer: one cage-spec ladder, priced by the £, projected onto workloads (cage-tier), humans and devices (break-glass), and model actions (the twin). Retire access.py's static table — break-glass.py already documents itself as its upgrade path.
corrections: Narrow to: access.py is superseded-but-undeleted dead code (never wired into any live decision path, only its own selfcheck) — a cleanup item, not a substantive four-way ladder conflict. The workload-plane pair (cage.py/enforce.py) is already explicitly reconciled into one ladder in platform/graded/README.md, and twin/enforcement-grades.yaml's unpriced design is already explained and tied to a concrete instantiation in its own header comments.

findings.title: The twin's ladder structurally forbids the mechanism the owner described
findings.claim: twin/enforcement.py enforces an invariant that fails validation if any rung of the enforcement ladder carries a number, which makes the owner's 'deny is the bottom rung, reached by the £' unrepresentable in the twin — the arm the twin phase called the system's intelligence.
findings.evidence: twin/enforcement-grades.yaml header: 'No rung carries a number, and the loader refuses one... A reduction per rung would be a free multiplier: tighten the rung, earn more credit, with nothing evidencing it... so the ladder orders consequence and prices nothing.' twin/enforcement.py:80-81 ('The only numeric field a rung may carry. Anything else numeric would be a price on a rung, and a price on a rung is credit nobody evidenced'), :176-183 raises on any priced field, exported as GRADE_NEVER_PRICES. The estate's cage.py does exactly what the twin forbids: every tier carries reduce and cost. Owner 2026-08-21: 'its never an exemption it'll be a informed caging based on risk appetite/threat intel' — informed means priced.
findings.recommendation: The twin's objection is sound about free credit and wrong about pricing. Keep the ban on a rung asserting its own mitigation, and separately let the rung carry the £ cost of occupying it (cage.py's cost, not its reduce) so the twin can compare a cage against an HR lever in the one currency the owner asked for.
corrections: The twin does not forbid pricing the mechanism the owner described; it forbids pricing it on the abstract rung definition (which would grant unevidenced credit for merely tightening a label) while pricing it correctly on the concrete control/response instance, in the same £ unit as everything else. No owner quote says "deny is the bottom rung, reached by the £" — that phrase is fabricated/misattributed. This finding should be refuted, not acted on as written.

findings.title: CONTEXT.md, the domain authority, still teaches the gate as a co-equal primitive
findings.claim: The repo's single domain doc defines Gate as 'a locked door… a hard admission block', instructs that the system must support both gates and lane-keeping, maps Deny=gate, defines semver by 'a pass into a fail at the gate' and asserts 'Compliant means admitted' — five statements a reader would take as the model, all predicated on the binary the owner abolished on 2026-08-22.
findings.evidence: CONTEXT.md:71-81 ('Lane-keeping vs. gate (the mea-culpa's load-bearing distinction)… Gate ("a locked door") — A hard admission block reserved for the catastrophic minority… The system must support BOTH… Audit = lane-keeping; Deny = gate'); CONTEXT.md:118-124 ('major = any change that can turn a pass into a fail at the gate… Compliant means admitted'); CONTEXT.md:195 ('Orphan guard — A deterministic catch-all ValidatingPolicy that denies at admission'). .scratch/computed-semver/spec.md:210-214 already carries the corrected model, so CONTEXT.md contradicts the project's own spec, not only the owner. DECISION_AUDIT P021 raised exactly this and it was never actioned.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the Lane-keeping-vs-gate entry as a cage-spec ladder with lane-keeping at the permissive end and refusal as the degenerate rung, and restate the semver entry in the cage-spec terms the release gate already computes in. A one-file edit that stops the most-read document teaching the abolished model.

findings.title: The canonical model diagram still draws a single admission neck and an exemptions ledger
findings.claim: .scratch/talk-spec/the-whole-model.md still renders 'the neck — one admission decision' with 'ENFORCEMENT / ADMISSION — Audit = observe · Deny = block' at the waist of the hourglass, and an 'EXEMPTIONS LEDGER' node described as 'priced · scoped · expiring · versioned' — the concept banned by name and a time condition ADR-0006 forbids.
findings.evidence: .scratch/talk-spec/the-whole-model.md:70-77 (neck subgraph) and :82 (the ledger node), :109-110 (the neck class applied to dist/shiftleft/admission). Owner 2026-08-20: 'there must never be an exemption ledger EVER, this is a banned concept explicitly, everything is codified'. CONTEXT.md:53-61 and pitch-v6 narration segment 13 both already say there is no exemption anywhere in the system, so this file contradicts every other artefact as well. DECISION_AUDIT P001, verdict reverse.
