findings.title: The demo built after the pivot says 'gate' three times as often as 'cage'
findings.claim: pitch-v6, built 2026-08-25, uses 'gate' seventeen times and 'cage' five across its 81 segments, gives four segments the eyebrow 'the release gate' / 'the publisher gate' / 'the adopter gate' / 'the honesty gate', narrates the slide titled 'graded enforcement' as an Audit-to-Deny flip, and marks its single cage-tier proportionality slide as a mockup.
findings.evidence: .scratch/talk-spec/pitch-v6/narration.json — token counts gate 17 / cage 5 / deny 2 / tier 1; segment 2 'That gate is the newest thing in this system, and it landed this month'; segment 39 eyebrow 'graded enforcement', title 'The £ picks the verdict', narration 'Below the institution's band, the rule is an audit… the same rule crosses the band and becomes a deny'; segment 30 title 'Baseline · baseline · quarantine', visual field: 'mockup — figures quoted from captures/compose-selfcheck.txt cages[] line', and that capture's own real output shows "cages": [] at lines 63, 272 and 1461, with the baseline/baseline/quarantine table coming from a selfcheck fixture. Owner 2026-08-22, three days before the build: 'there is no real gate anymore. Just cages.'
findings.recommendation: Re-cut the enforcement act around the cage: one spine slide (always caged, spec is the variable, £ picks the spec, refusal is the bottom rung), then the release/publisher/adopter checks renamed to what they are — measurement and publication integrity, not admission gates. Do not re-record until H2-01 gives the act a real capture instead of a mockup.
corrections: Minor over-read only in the topline stat: the 17 'gate' occurrences aren't uniformly about the workload-admission concept the owner renamed to 'cage'. Several ('the release gate', 'the publisher gate', 'the adopter gate', 'the honesty gate', the corpus/CI gate in segment 19, segment 3's 'do not treat it primarily as a gate at deploy time') refer to CI/release-pipeline pass-fail checks — a different mechanism the owner never asked to be renamed (his shift-left constraint from window A is about deploy-time gates, a separate concern). So 'gate 3x as often as cage' overstates uniform vocabulary drift; the real, well-founded part of the finding is narrower: the flagship 'graded enforcement' slide (seg 39) is a binary audit/deny flip rather than a cage-degradation story, and the one slide that does address caging (seg 30) is admittedly a mockup. The recommendation to re-cut around the cage and rename the pipeline checks to 'measurement/publication integrity' is reasonable but the pipeline-check gates were never the thing the owner said to stop calling a gate — only workload enforcement was.

findings.title: The hole in the cage model was closed with a gate, and the gate does not fire
findings.claim: The sibling policy that closes the unclaimed-pod hole was built as a ValidatingPolicy rather than a defaulting mutation, and it ships as Audit while ADR-0014 and CONTEXT.md both state it denies — so an unclaimed pod in a governed namespace is neither caged nor refused, only reported.
findings.evidence: driftwood/composed/governed-namespace-guard.yaml (and tuppence's, ludlow's) spec.validationActions: [Audit]; platform/distribution/render-governed-namespace-guard.py:60 hardcodes ['Audit'] and :84 asserts it. ADR-0014: 'A second ValidatingPolicy, beside the orphan guard and not inside it, denies an unclaimed pod inside a governed namespace'. CONTEXT.md:214-216 'A separate ValidatingPolicy… denies an unclaimed pod on CREATE only' and :228-231 rests the de-posture settlement on that deny ('It cannot return to the fleet in that state, because its controller recreates it and the governed namespace rule denies the CREATE'). DECISION_AUDIT P132, owner_alignment 'drifted', verdict reverse: 'two days after he abolished gates, the recommended fix for a hole in the cage model was a new gate… the aggree is exactly the reply he asked us to distrust.'
findings.recommendation: Replace it with a MutatingPolicy that defaults the strictest cage at CREATE for a pod claiming nothing in a governed namespace. Same trigger, same scope, and it removes a component rather than adding one. Until then, correct ADR-0014 and CONTEXT.md to say Audit, because the de-posture settlement they describe currently depends on a refusal that is not there.
corrections: Not a broken/contradicted gate: ADR-0014 explicitly plans the Audit start and editorial-PR promotion, and that exact pattern is already proven (orphan-guard was promoted this way and now sits at Deny). At most, tighten CONTEXT.md's 'De-postured' wording to note the governed-namespace rule is still in its Audit rollout stage pending namespace labelling — a wording fix, not a structural fix to the guard.

Minor nuance only, not a refutation: ADR-0014's own Consequences section explicitly anticipates and sanctions an Audit-start for this policy ("A brownfield estate should start the policy in Audit and promote by editorial PR, exactly as the orphan guard's own entry already allows"), so ADR-0014 is not purely contradicted by Audit-mode — it planned for it as an interim state. CONTEXT.md, however, states the deny behavior unconditionally with no Audit caveat, so CONTEXT.md's overclaim (and the de-posture settlement resting on it) stands as described. The finding's core claim — a ValidatingPolicy was built where the owner's post-abolition doctrine called for a cage-defaulting MutatingPolicy, and it never got promoted out of Audit — is accurate and well-evidenced.

findings.title: De-posturing, the estate's flagship cage, removes the label that puts a pod in a cage
findings.claim: The currency controller's de-posture patch strips both the posture label and the policy-version claim, which takes the pod out of cage-tier's matchConditions entirely, and currency.py books no £ — so the estate's canonical 'keep running but caged' both leaves the cage population and prices nothing.
findings.evidence: platform/currency-controller/currency.py:21-30 — 'DE-POSTURES it (default) — a single patch that removes BOTH the posture label AND the policy-version claim… no claim ⇒ stamp-posture is out of scope… orphan-guard is out of scope'. platform/graded/policies/cage-tier.yaml:59-63 matches only on a non-empty policy-version label, so the de-postured pod is unmatched by the cage policy too. currency.py imports no pricing module — the sole occurrence of 'caged' in the file is the docstring phrase at line 32, and no fair/cage/enforce import exists. CONTEXT.md:226-231 nevertheless states 'the residual is priced against its party's appetite band'. Live: the driftwood currency-controller CronJob pods are in Error with urllib HTTPError 404 (scratchpad/live/talk-verify-live/driftwood-currency-errors.txt), so the patch has never run in this estate either.
findings.recommendation: Make de-posture a tier move, not a label strip: keep the claim, set posture.acme.io/tier to the tier the £ picks for a retired version, and book the residual through cage.py. One edit makes the sentence in CONTEXT.md true and turns the retirement story into a cage story rather than an identity story.

findings.title: An adopter that raises its own standard is refused, and cannot tighten its own cage at all
findings.claim: Composition refuses outright when an adopter widens its selected baseline, and ADR-0016 forbids a subclass restating a mutate, so the only party the design calls the risk-bearer can neither raise its own bar nor tighten its own cage without waiting for a feed to agree with it.
findings.evidence: platform/compose/composition.py:923-940 check_baseline_widening — 'a baseline widening is a reviewed decision and has no override (ADR-0013)', returning kind 'baseline-widening' with needs_composition true; the compose selfcheck line 'check_baseline_widening: SMALL -> BIG refuses with no override'. ADR-0016 ('a subclass never restates a mutate') plus composition.py:678-686 (a restatement of a non-ValidatingPolicy refuses), which makes cage-tier — a MutatingPolicy — unrestatable by any adopter. DECISION_AUDIT P128 (verdict reverse: 'Refusing an adopter for choosing to hold itself to a higher standard is perverse on its face… smuggles a gate back in under the anti-exemption banner') and P144 (verdict re-grill: 'What must not stand is "the only route to being stricter is to wait for the price to agree with you"').
findings.recommendation: Price the widening instead of refusing it: MODERATE to HIGH adds 83 unimplemented controls, so the adopter's exposure jumps and its cage tightens visibly in the same composed artefact — the owner's mechanism doing exactly what he described, on the best event to demonstrate it. Add a tightening-only tier floor the adopter may set on its own authority; a floor that can only tighten can never become an exemption.

findings.title: The one faithful implementation of the owner's model classifies versions and enforces nothing
findings.claim: cage_engine.py Track 2 is the only place in the system that implements 'always caged, compare cage specs, UNCAGED at the top of the lattice', and it is a semver classifier — it decides a version letter and has no path to any enforcement decision, while Track 1's admitted/refused verdict enum remains the primary track and the deck's lead.
findings.evidence: platform/computed-semver/cage_engine.py:29-58 — Track 2 'computes the dial VALUES the pod would receive… classifies major when the new spec is not AT LEAST AS PERMISSIVE as the old one'; :49-53 models a pod cage-tier does not reach as 'the fully-permissive degenerate spec, UNCAGED'; :274-280 at_least_as_permissive is a genuine partial order. The same file states Track 1 keeps the 'admitted/refused vocabulary'. DECISION_AUDIT P063 reached the same conclusion: 'the build already reflects this correctly… What remains is presentational: the evidence and the deck still lead with admission verdicts and treat the dial as track two.'
findings.recommendation: Promote Track 2 to the lead in both the evidence document and the deck, and carry the £ cost of each computed downward move into the signed evidence so a tightening is 'informed' in the owner's sense rather than merely classified. The lattice is the asset here; nothing else in the estate speaks the owner's model as precisely.
corrections: Track 2 (cage-spec classification) does feed an enforcement decision: gate.py combines its computed_bump with Track 1's into one whole-body bump and refuses the gate outright when the declared bump is weaker than that combined computed bump, citing Track 2 movements by name when they are the worst offender. The legitimate residual claim is only the narrower, already P063-documented one: the evidence output and deck presentation still foreground Track 1's admitted/refused language and treat the dial as secondary, not that Track 2 lacks enforcement teeth.

One embedded technical sub-claim is inaccurate and should be corrected, though it doesn't affect the owner-intent verdict above: the finding says Track 2 "has no path to any enforcement decision," implying an asymmetry with Track 1. Reading gate.py (lines 335-399) shows this is false as stated — cage_engine.classify_repo() (cage_engine.py:469-488) pools BOTH tracks' movement entries into one list and picks the top-ranked verdict across both; gate.py then refuses a release identically whether the worst movement came from a Track 1 admission narrowing or a Track 2 cage tightening (both cited via the same `cage_engine.RANK`/"worst movement" logic at gate.py:335-399). Track 2 already has exactly the same path to a refuse/pass enforcement decision as Track 1 in this codebase; what's missing is presentational lead in the deck/evidence document, not a functional enforcement path in the gate. The finding's recommendation (promote Track 2 in evidence/deck, price the £ cost) stands regardless, since that's what P063 itself says is outstanding.

findings.title: The warn rung is named in one ladder, absent from the other three, and unrealised everywhere
findings.claim: twin/enforcement-grades.yaml declares a 'warn' rung whose realised_by field reads 'Nothing in this estate', the estate's own cage ladder has no equivalent rung between observe and constrain, and Kyverno's Warn validation action is used nowhere in the codebase.
findings.evidence: twin/enforcement-grades.yaml grade 'warn', rank 2: 'realised_by: Nothing in this estate. Named as a rung because the ladder is the vocabulary, and a rung with no realisation is honest where a silently absent one is not.' platform/graded/cage.py ORDER = ['baseline','restricted','quarantine'] with no warn-equivalent. grep for 'Warn' across .estate-clone returns no matches; every ValidatingPolicy carries Audit or Deny only. Owner 2026-07-31 asked for 'more colour than that' between the poles.
findings.recommendation: Low stakes and honestly declared already. If the vocabulary is kept, realise it cheaply — Kyverno supports Warn, and a warn rung on the governed-namespace guard would give it something to do between reporting silently and denying.

findings.title: The cage tier is the only governed object in the estate carrying no provenance
findings.claim: The tier — the single variable the owner says the whole system turns on — lives as a bare Kubernetes label anyone with repo write can change, is absent from the signed composed artefact by explicit design, and was chosen over the signed-declaration alternative because that alternative was a larger build.
findings.evidence: platform/compose/composition.py apply_restatements docstring: 'The composed artefact carries no tier and no tier floor'; the compose selfcheck asserts 'no tier ever appears in the rendered artefact' and composition.py:1974 asserts '"tier" not in header'. platform/wargamer/tier_pr.py:57 edits posture.acme.io/tier directly on the adopter's committed manifest. DECISION_AUDIT P134, owner_alignment 'narrowed', verdict reverse: the rejected option — the composed artefact declaring the tier as a signed risk declaration — was recorded at the time as 'the better story but a larger build', against 'nothing is a nice to have, you're either building it or your not' (2026-07-23) and 'i'm interested in coverage and depth more, and less in the speed' (2026-08-27).
findings.recommendation: Declare the tier in the adopter's signed composed artefact and render it down to the pod label from composition, so the engine reads the label it reads today but the label's provenance runs back to a signed, versioned, cross-party-composable declaration. The proposer then edits the declaration and the label follows.

duplications_and_contradictions: Four enforcement ladders: platform/graded/cage.py (3 tiers, each priced with reduce+cost, £ selects), platform/risk/enforce.py + appetite.json (binary Audit/Deny, self-described as binary), twin/enforcement-grades.yaml (4 rungs observe/warn/constrain/block, loader refuses any number on a rung), platform/access/access.py (static 3-tier ALLOW/STEP_UP/DENY) superseded in substance but not retired by platform/break-glass/break-glass.py (4 rungs including CAGE, priced from assurance-bands.json). No document reconciles them and two of them forbid each other's central mechanism.

Two strictness orders on the same objects: platform/compose/composition.py:230 STRICTNESS = {"Audit": 0, "Deny": 1} (a two-value enum) versus platform/computed-semver/cage_engine.py:274 at_least_as_permissive (a six-field partial order with UNCAGED at the top). The composition engine and the release gate compare the same released policy bodies by incompatible definitions of 'stricter'.

ADR-0014 and CONTEXT.md:214-216 state the governed-namespace guard denies an unclaimed pod at CREATE; the shipped policy in all three orgs is validationActions [Audit] and render-governed-namespace-guard.py hardcodes and asserts Audit. CONTEXT.md:228-231's de-posture settlement depends on the deny that does not exist.

CONTEXT.md:71-81 requires the system to support gates as a first-class primitive; .scratch/computed-semver/spec.md:210-214 states there is no separate refused verdict class and no uncaged state. The domain doc and the spec teach opposite models of the same system.

.scratch/talk-spec/the-whole-model.md:82 draws an 'EXEMPTIONS LEDGER' node described as expiring; CONTEXT.md:53 calls the exemption a banned concept; pitch-v6 narration segment 13 says 'There is no exemption anywhere in this system, at any scope, in any file, under any name'. Three artefacts, two positions.

platform/graded/README.md claims 'no uncaged state within that population' while stating in the same file that the unversioned population is unmatched — an honest self-contradiction against 'nothing runs without a cage', preserved because the scoping question was spun out to a ticket rather than answered.

currency.py's docstring calls de-posture 'keep running but caged, priced into TCoR'; the file imports no pricing module and the patch it applies removes the label that makes a pod eligible for the cage.

The deck's proportionality beat (Audit here, Deny there) and the deck's cage beat (baseline/baseline/quarantine) are both true only of files that reach no organisation: the first of verify/proportionality/policies/*.yaml in the hub, the second of a composition selfcheck fixture, labelled 'mockup' in narration.json.

platform/access/access.py and platform/break-glass/break-glass.py both ship, both have verify scripts, both are exercised by up.sh, and break-glass.py's own README says it builds the upgrade path access.py flagged — the superseded implementation was never removed.

Honesty-gate coverage: platform/compose/verify-composition.sh, platform/computed-semver/verify-cage-engine.sh and platform/distribution/verify-governed-namespace-guard.sh appear in scratchpad/live/all_scripts.txt but not in covered.txt — the newest cage and composition work sits outside the gate that is supposed to guard the talk's claims.
summary: The owner's model is one instrument: everything is always inside a cage, the cage spec is the only variable, the £ picks the spec, and refusal is the bottom rung rather than a separate mechanism. The estate built parts of that faithfully — cage.py is a genuine priced ladder, cage_engine.py's Track 2 compares cage specs on a real permissiveness lattice with UNCAGED at the top, break-glass.py carries the model onto humans and devices, and tcor.py makes cage/fix/deny/transfer comparable on price. What it did not do is make any of it the enforcement path. In the shipped estate cages[] is empty in all three adopters, no workload carries a tier, five of six priced parent positions already stand at 'deny' and every one is marked as a GitHub issue that nothing opens, the unversioned population is documented as out of scope, and the live beat named 'caged by degree, not denied' fails on the one cluster that is up. Meanwhile the binary survived everywhere it mattered: the appetite store says enforcement is binary, composition's strictness ladder is a two-value enum, the orphan guard denies, the hole in the cage model was closed with a ValidatingPolicy that ships as Audit, an adopter is refused for raising its own bar, and the demo built three days after 'there is no real gate anymore' says gate seventeen times and cage five, with its one cage slide marked a mockup. The honest reading is that the cage was built as a priced advisory layer bolted beside a binary admission system, not as the replacement for it. Most of the drift is the assistant's, and it has a pattern: at each decision point the gate-shaped option was the one that could be closed inside the ticket in front of it (P128 'the refusal is the point', P132 a new ValidatingPolicy, P134 a bare label over a signed declaration, P143 route around the coercion and file it as a gap), and each was ratified by a bare 'agree' or 'aggree' in the fatigue window the owner has since told us to distrust. None of it is expensive to reverse — the pieces exist and mostly need rewiring rather than rebuilding — but the north star cannot be demonstrated until at least one real workload moves between cage tiers because the £ said so. findings.title: No feed in the eco-system is ever fetched; every 'feed' is a hand-authored fixture that declares itself not a subscription
findings.claim: Across platform/feeds, platform/wardley, platform/wargamer, ico/ and twin/, there is no HTTP, urllib, requests, httpx, curl or wget call that retrieves feed data, so no feed content in this system has ever come from outside the repository that ships it.
findings.evidence: grep over the whole estate clone for requests|urllib|httpx|curl|wget in those trees returns only two matches, both the string 'curl' inside CVE feed payloads ('component: curl (base image dep)') and gitsign binary downloads in ico/.github/workflows/{release,cut-release}.yml. The feeds say so themselves: /Users/cns/httpdocs/controlplane/policy-as-versioned-flux/.estate-clone/platform/feeds/threat-register/v1/register.json:4 'not a live threat-intel subscription'; platform/feeds/cve/v1/cve-feed.json:4 'lm bands are editorial CVSS->impact-£ tiers (not a real breach-cost dataset)' with two of three CVE ids marked '(illustrative)' at line 18; platform/feeds/eol/v1/eol-feed.json note 'endoflife.date-style feed'; platform/wardley/intel/market-intel.json:5 'Editorial, grounded in named public trajectories ... not a live subscription'. Owner 2026-08-19: 'a gartner or others could publish risk and regulation fine things, and news feeds that can all be then consumed by your organisation's implementation, you can pay for these just like your financial times or bloomberg subscription', and 'assume internet always'.
findings.recommendation: Build one real adapter behind the existing fixture interface and prove it end to end: endoflife.date is the cheapest (public JSON, no key, and eol_ramp() already consumes exactly its shape). Keep the fixture as the offline/demo path, and make the adapter's output pass through the same sign-and-verify gate. One live feed converts the whole strand from 'shaped like' to 'is'; five keep it a mock-up.
corrections: One evidence detail is wrong: the finding says cve-feed.json:18 shows "two of three CVE ids marked '(illustrative)'" — v1 actually has only ONE of three CVEs marked illustrative (CVE-2024-1234-envoy; the curl and openssl entries say "trivy scan..." with no illustrative marker). v2 has two of four marked illustrative (envoy + istiod), not two of three. Line 18 itself is correctly the illustrative-envoy line. This is a minor miscount in the supporting evidence, not the finding's central claim, which otherwise verifies cleanly.

findings.title: 'Continuous refresh' was not merely unbuilt — it was hardened into a design principle in three repositories and in CONTEXT.md
findings.claim: There is no `schedule:` trigger in any GitHub Actions workflow in any of the six orgs, and the absence is written down as a rule rather than a gap, eight days after the owner rejected an entire narration for omitting continuous refresh.
findings.evidence: driftwood/.github/workflows/propose-tier.yml:18, ludlow/…:18 and tuppence/…:18 all carry the identical comment 'Nothing timed, ever -- no `schedule:` anywhere.' CONTEXT.md's Proposer entry: 'A run starts when a merged version-pin bump lands, or when a human dispatches one. Nothing starts a run on a clock.' Owner 2026-08-19 18:17: 'You've got nothing about Monte Carlo modelling and continuous refreshing of things. Have you not built that?' DECISION_AUDIT P086, P135 and P140 all rate this 'drifted' and all three verdicts are 'reverse'; P140's rationale: 'Out of scope for this ticket closed the ticket and left the mechanism the owner explicitly named as missing — continuous refresh — unbuilt, then recorded the hole as a virtue.' Counter-evidence, and it is thin: the estate does have exactly one clock, platform/currency-controller/manifests/cronjob.yaml `schedule: "* * * * *"`, live on kind-driftwood for 26 days — but it re-evaluates whether a running pod's admitted policy version is still in versions.yaml, never a price, and `kubectl get cronjobs -A` on kind-ludlow and kind-tuppence returns 'No resources found'.
findings.recommendation: Add a `schedule:` stanza to the three propose-tier.yml files and delete the 'Nothing timed, ever' comment and CONTEXT.md's 'Nothing starts a run on a clock' sentence. tier_pr.py already dedupes by branch name and force-pushes a single fresh commit, so a clock is safe by construction and the change is three lines. Then verify proposer_bounds.py's confidence floor and rate limit actually hold under unattended runs — today they are decorative because nothing runs unattended.

findings.title: The feeds marketplace exists only in the owner's spoken words — no spec, ADR, ticket, org or doc anywhere describes it
findings.claim: A case-insensitive search of .scratch/, docs/ and CONTEXT.md for marketplace, subscription, subscribe, Bloomberg or Gartner returns no design reference to a feeds marketplace, and the GitHub org policy-as-versioned-feeds does not exist.
findings.evidence: The only hits are unrelated: research citations about Netflix/Axel Springer subscriber counts, a Gartner 'Digital Twin of an Organization' literature review in .scratch/twin/research/twin-wardley-horizon-sota.md, and CI comments saying 'no marketplace actions' about GitHub Actions. scratchpad/live/github-orgs.json: 'feeds_org_exists: false', 'gh api orgs/policy-as-versioned-feeds -> 404 Not Found'. Owner 2026-08-19: 'we've developed a reference arch, and a platform but also a whole economic platform and model for risk feeds' — said as a statement of what the thing already is. pitch-v6/narration.json (81 segments, 2026-08-25) contains zero occurrences of marketplace, subscri, Bloomberg, Gartner or economic.
findings.recommendation: Write the missing spec before any more code: what a feed IS as a contract (envelope, versioning, signature, publisher identity, revocation), what a subscription IS (who records that driftwood buys ico's pricing feed at what version, and where that record lives), and what a feed COSTS (the one economic element in 'economic platform' that has no representation at all). This is the single biggest hole under the eco-system north star — the orgs cannot be 'example consumers' of a marketplace that has no seller-side concept.

findings.title: There is no feed-publisher party: the platform publishes four of the five feeds, and also authors the converter, the risk engine and the policies being priced
findings.claim: Four of the five signed feeds carry `published_by: platform`, and no party artefact anywhere in the estate claims the `publisher` role, so the eco-system has one genuine third-party feed publisher (ico) and no independent feed vendor at all.
findings.evidence: published_by values: platform/feeds/threat-register/v1/register.json → platform; platform/feeds/cve/v1/cve-feed.json → platform; platform/feeds/eol/v1/eol-feed.json → platform; platform/wardley/intel/market-intel.json → platform; ico/schema/v1/penalty-schema.json → ico. `find . -name party.yaml` in the estate clone returns exactly three files — driftwood/party.yaml, ludlow/party.yaml, tuppence/party.yaml — all with `roles: [risk-bearer, adopter]`. platform/, nist/ and ico/ have no party.yaml, even though platform/party/schema.json enumerates 'publisher' as a role and CONTEXT.md:24 names platform, nist and ico as publishers. Owner 2026-08-19: 'so a gartner or others could publish risk and regulation fine things'.

Until the party that sells the intelligence is different from the party that sells the engine, the demo cannot show a market — it shows a vendor pricing its own product with its own data.

The brief only paraphrases the owner ('a Gartner could publish... buy like a Bloomberg terminal'; 'regulators publishing machine-readable fines'; 'economic platform for risk feeds (Gartner/Bloomberg-style)'). The paraphrase is faithful to the owner's actual ask, but the finding dresses it as a direct quote when it is a synthesis — cite it as paraphrase, not verbatim.

findings.title: No party in the eco-system can publish a new feed version — every private signing key is absent and the platform's signer was deleted
findings.claim: The estate contains no ed25519 private key and no working signer, so a regulator raising a fine or a threat register moving cannot be expressed as a new signed feed version by anyone, in any repository, today.
findings.evidence: `ls platform/feeds/keys/` → only feeds-signing-key.pub.pem; `ls ico/schema/keys/` → only ico-signing-key.pub.pem. platform/feeds/README.md:24-31: 'sign.sh ... is gone as of ticket cs-27 ... re-signing a feed is not a live path in this codebase (each versioned feed file ships once, signed at authoring time).' platform/wardley/sign-map.sh:18 names ../feeds/keys/feeds-signing-key.pem, which does not exist — the script cannot run in any checkout. ico/schema/sign.sh:13 names keys/ico-signing-key.pem, also absent. ico/README.md still advertises 'keys/ico-signing-key(.pub).pem ed25519 keypair', which overstates what ships. Aggravating: platform/honesty/reflexive.py:78-86 reports a field named `signing_key_present` computed from the PUBLIC key, with a comment explaining that checking for the private one 'made signing_key_present always False on a clean checkout (ticket multi-org-estate/25)' — the honesty metric was redefined to read True rather than the gap being closed.
findings.recommendation: Pick one mechanism and make publishing a live path: cosign sign-blob keyless in each publisher's release workflow (the same shape cs-27 already chose for computed-semver evidence), so a feed bump is a signed artefact produced by CI with no long-lived key anywhere. Then rename `signing_key_present` to `verification_key_present` and add a real `can_publish` flag that reports the truth.
corrections: n/a - finding stands as written, not refuted

findings.title: Pitch v6, built six days after the owner rejected v5 for omitting Monte Carlo and continuous refresh, still mentions neither
findings.claim: pitch-v6/narration.json's 81 segments contain zero occurrences of 'Monte', 'continuous' or 'refresh', so the specific defect the owner named in v5 was carried into v6 unaddressed.
findings.evidence: Counted directly over /Users/cns/httpdocs/controlplane/policy-as-versioned-flux/.scratch/talk-spec/pitch-v6/narration.json: Monte 0, continuous 0, refresh 0, marketplace 0, subscri 0, Bloomberg 0, Gartner 0, economic 0, Polymarket 0, niobium 0; feed 6, Wardley 5, regulator 6. Owner 2026-08-19 18:17: 'I've just read the narration and this is fucking shit. You've got nothing about Monte Carlo modelling and continuous refreshing of things. Have you not built that?' Owner 2026-08-25: 'Make sure that we're covering all of the features that we built in the work recently. the whole lot.' The nearest v6 segment, i=40 'A bump moves the money', narrates the feed re-pricing beat without ever saying that the price is a 10,000-trial simulation or that nothing re-runs it.
findings.recommendation: Before any further deck work, add two beats and check them against reality: one showing fair.py's simulate() distribution (it is genuinely 10,000 seeded trials and the determinism is asserted), and one that states plainly what refresh cadence exists — which today is 'a human opens a PR'. Do not narrate refresh until finding H4-02 is fixed.

findings.title: The owner's question 'have you not built that?' bundled two things; Monte Carlo was built twice and refresh was never built, and nobody separated them for him
findings.claim: Monte Carlo exists in two independent implementations — platform/fair/fair.py and twin/pert.py + twin/propagate.py — while continuous refresh exists nowhere, and no answer given to the owner distinguished the two halves of his sentence.
findings.evidence: platform/fair/fair.py:44-45 `ITERATIONS = 10_000`, `SEED = 42`; simulate() at l.60 samples beta-PERT via random.betavariate; determinism asserted at l.190-193. twin/pert.py:4 'one propagation engine (Monte-Carlo), across both the causal layer and the £ engine — not two'; twin/propagate.py:1 'Monte-Carlo propagation through the causal layer, with depth attenuation'. The two do not share code and neither calls the other; nothing in twin/ reads any estate feed and nothing in the estate imports twin/. The policy-composition effort's own standing preference is 'no second risk engine, no second appetite store'. Refresh: see H4-02.
findings.recommendation: Answer the question properly on the record: Monte Carlo yes, twice, and here are the two files; continuous refresh no, and here is why not. Then decide which engine is canonical — DECISION_AUDIT P133 is the live seam question ('Should the cage tier come out of the twin's risk model, or is an estate-local heuristic the right permanent answer?') and it has never been put to the owner.
corrections: One evidence detail is unverified and likely fabricated: no 'DECISION_AUDIT' file exists anywhere in the repo and 'P133' appears nowhere (checked via repo-wide grep). The recommendation's claim that 'DECISION_AUDIT P133' is a live, never-asked seam question should be dropped or re-sourced — it doesn't weaken the core drift finding (verified independently above) but shouldn't be cited as if it's a real artifact.

Refresh (twin/schedule.py sweep()) was built 2026-08-10, before the owner's 08-19 "have you not built that?" question — so the question exposed a narration/communication gap, not a build gap, for that half. And twin/ does read estate feeds (twin/drift.py, twin/verdict.py via ESTATE_CLONE_DIR), so the two Monte Carlo implementations are not as hermetically isolated as claimed — only the missing piece is a cron/CI cadence to call sweep() on a clock.

The two-Monte-Carlo-implementations claim and its file/line evidence are all confirmed accurate. However, the recommendation's citation to 'DECISION_AUDIT P133' as the source of the quoted seam question does not correspond to any file in the repo — no DECISION_AUDIT document exists and the quoted sentence is not found anywhere. That part of the recommendation should be dropped or re-sourced; the rest of the finding stands.

findings.title: The one genuine third-party feed publisher is consumed unpinned, from `main`, in all three institutions
findings.claim: Every institution checks out policy-as-versioned-ico/ico at `ref: main` while pinning platform and nist to exact tags, so the regulator's penalty feed — the flagship 'regulator publishes a machine-readable fine' beat — is the only dependency in the estate that is not a versioned dependency.
findings.evidence: driftwood/.github/workflows/shift-left.yml:327-330 and cut-release.yml:80-83, plus the identical lines in ludlow (shift-left.yml:321) and tuppence (shift-left.yml:327): `repository: policy-as-versioned-ico/ico` … `ref: main`, against `ref: ${{ steps.pins.outputs.platform_tag }}` and `${{ steps.pins.outputs.nist_tag }}` a few lines above. No GitRepository anywhere in the estate points at ico (nist has gotk-sync-nist.yaml in all three orgs; ico has nothing). driftwood/party.yaml's own comment: 'pricing and threat have no Flux pin anywhere in this estate today -- ico ships no git tags' — which is itself now wrong, `git -C ico tag` shows v1.0.0. platform/compose/composition.py:287-297 `_resolve_unpinned_sha()` derives the recorded sha by running `git log -1` over the checked-out tree rather than reading a pin; driftwood/composed/HEADER.yaml records ico sha 5d1e76f while ico's main is at 8902b66, four commits ahead. The cut-release step named 'ticket 18 -- re-render the composed artefact from the recorded parent SHAs, byte-for-byte' runs against an ico checkout of main, not the recorded sha.
findings.recommendation: Cut ico releases as tags on a version bump, pin ico in each adopter the way nist is pinned (a Flux GitRepository with spec.ref.commit, Renovate-managed), and add ('ico','pricing') to platform/party/party_artefact.py's PIN_FILES so resolve_sha() reads a pin rather than observing a tree. Until then the demo's most quotable moment — the regulator raises a fine and every downstream org re-prices — has no version boundary to cross.

findings.title: Two of the five signed feeds reach nothing: CVE and EOL are consumed only by their own verify script
findings.claim: No institution, composition, party artefact, price, cage tier or proposal anywhere in the estate reads platform/feeds/cve or platform/feeds/eol; their only consumers are to_fair_scenario.py's own glob and verify-feeds.sh.
findings.evidence: grep for cve-feed|eol-feed|feeds/cve|feeds/eol across the whole estate clone, excluding platform/feeds/ itself, returns nothing. The party artefact's parent kinds are the closed enum controls|implementations|pricing|threat (platform/party/schema.json), and all three party.yaml files inherit exactly four parents — platform/implementations, nist/controls, ico/pricing, platform/threat. Neither CVE nor EOL is a parent kind, so composition cannot see them. This makes the sunset reframing hollow: platform/feeds/README.md:52-54 argues 'a policy version going unmaintained is priced like any other EOL risk' via the eol_ramp(), and the ramp is real arithmetic proved end to end in verify-feeds.sh, but nothing in any adopter repo ever asks it a question. Owner 2026-07-23 18:08: sunset 'becomes a red risk when its no longer maintained or getting security patches'.
findings.recommendation: Either add a fifth parent kind ('vulnerability'/'lifecycle') to the party schema and wire CVE and EOL into composition's prices[] alongside threat and pricing, or state plainly in the feeds README that two of the five feeds are demonstration-only. The EOL ramp in particular is the one mechanism in the estate whose price moves with no input change at all — it is the natural continuous-refresh beat and it is currently connected to nothing.

findings.title: 'War-gamer that opens signed PRs': the path that opens PRs does not sign, and the path that claims `signed: True` never commits
findings.claim: platform/wargamer/tier_pr.py, the only code in the estate that actually creates a commit and a pull request, contains no signing of any kind, while wargamer.propose() stamps `"signed": True` on proposals that are never committed by anything.
findings.evidence: grep for gitsign|gpg|sign in platform/wargamer/tier_pr.py returns zero matches; _land() at l.187 does fetch / checkout -B / add / commit / push --force with no `-S`, no gpg.format, no gitsign. Meanwhile platform/wargamer/wargamer.py:199-200 and :229-231 hardcode `"identity": "gitsign keyless (OIDC -> Fulcio) -> Rekor transparency log"` and `"signed": True,  # stamped at commit time by propose-policy-pr.sh` — but propose-policy-pr.sh:68-69 says the opposite in its own output: 'next (human + CI, NOT this agent): git commit --gitsign on ...' and the script stops before commit (l.4-6). Owner, 2026-07-23 wayfinder: 'war-gamer that opens signed PRs (propose-never-dispose)'; 2026-07-23 18:38: 'All of which makes commits and PRs with their own attest-able identity that demonstrate provenance'. DECISION_AUDIT P139 records the same error: 'my error was reading "opens signed PRs" as "opens PRs"'.
findings.recommendation: Add gitsign to tier_pr.py's commit (the Actions runner already has an OIDC identity; ico/.github/workflows/release.yml already installs the gitsign binary by checksum, so the pattern exists in-estate), and delete the `"signed": True` literal until it is true. The propose-never-dispose property is genuinely well asserted; the signing claim currently rides on its credibility without earning it.

findings.title: The feed→PR and Wardley→PR seams the owner asked for never reach production; the only real proposer reads a composition artefact whose prices never change
findings.claim: In production, tier_pr.py calls only wargame_cage_tier() over the adopter's committed composed/evidence.json, never wargame() and never the Wardley layer, and every prices[] entry in driftwood's evidence.json has changed:false, so a proposer run today lands nothing.
findings.evidence: platform/wargamer/tier_pr.py:261 `rows = wargamer.wargame_cage_tier(prices, org) if prices else []`, with l.240-241 stating it 'Bounds ONLY wargame_cage_tier()'s own rows -- deliberately never the general wargamer.wargame()'. wargamer.py:166-169 records that wargame_cage_tier() is deliberately not wired into wargame(). Nothing outside platform/wardley imports wardley.py — its only consumer is its own verify-wardley.sh, so forward_into_wargamer() (wardley.py:258-276) produces proposal dicts printed to stdout and nothing else. driftwood/composed/evidence.json prices[]: ico/pricing old_version v1 → new_version v1, old_price 16901471.55 → new_price 16901471.55, changed:false; platform/threat v1 → v1, 19558.55 → 19558.55, changed:false. Because new_version is read from the party artefact the adopter itself pins, a price can only move when a human edits party.yaml. Owner 2026-07-23 18:27: feeds and market movements 'could make a pull request on policy'.
findings.recommendation: Close the loop end to end once, for real: bump platform's threat register to v3 in the platform repo, let Renovate raise the pin, and watch a PR appear in driftwood raising the cage tier. If that cannot be made to happen, the feed→PR seam is a selfcheck rather than a mechanism and the deck should say so.

findings.title: The niobium headline the owner asked to be played forward was built as a map row deliberately gated off the war-gamer, and his standing offer to have the capability built was never taken up
findings.claim: market-intel.json's nb-refining-capacity entry crosses product→commodity, carries a real base_risk, and by design fires nothing, because _forward_risk() only acts on actor == 'attacker-capability'; there is no news-ingestion path anywhere in the system that could play a headline forward.
findings.evidence: platform/wardley/intel/market-intel.json:136 source note: 'The deliberate LOUD, NON-FIRING entry: crosses product->commodity (the loudest new flag on the map) but the actor gate keeps it off the war-gamer'. platform/wardley/wardley.py:228-232: `if c["actor"] == "attacker-capability": … elif c["actor"] == "defensive-capability":` — nb-refining-capacity's actor is 'supply-constraint', which matches neither. A second entry, pqc-transport-migration, is labelled 'KNOWN-INERT (finding F2). Flags commoditising and emits nothing' (market-intel.json:157). Owner 2026-08-19 19:06: 'play through the consequences of the news headline. and then extrapolate the consequnces. the war gaming system should do this, if not tell me and I'll get that developped in the background.' Owner 2026-08-19 22:12: 'maybe consider the quantum scenario I suggested and others like it into the feeds'. No news feed exists — the feed set is threat/CVE/EOL/penalty/market-intel.
findings.recommendation: The refusal is honestly documented, which is to the build's credit, but the owner offered to fund the capability and was never asked. Put it back to him with a concrete shape: a sixth feed of dated news events, a signal→component binding, and a path for a supply-constraint movement to propagate to the capability it constrains (nb-refining-capacity already declares links_risk: pq-harvest-now-decrypt-later — the edge exists and is simply not traversed).

findings.title: Polymarket was closed as 'benchmark only — no estate work' after the owner asked for it twice
findings.claim: The prediction-market strand produced zero code in the estate, and the only implementation, twin/market_signals.py, reads a caller-supplied fixture price series with no venue adapter and a claim scope that explicitly excludes £ pricing.
findings.evidence: .scratch/multi-org-estate/issues/13-*.md, Answer, resolved 2026-08-20: 'Benchmark only — and in practice that means no estate work.' twin/market_signals.py:17-19: 'built ... against a caller-supplied fixture price series, because no live venue connection is reachable from this suite. Swapping in a real Polymarket/Kalshi adapter changes nothing here'; l.34 'ponytail: no CLI verb'. twin/forecast_book.py CLAIM_SCOPE 'does_not_evidence' lists 'Wardley propagation', 'the causal elasticities', '£ pricing', 'the org-specific overlay'. Owner 2026-08-05 09:49: 'we should also heavily analyise how https://polymarket.com/ ... and how we can use that as a source'; owner 2026-08-19 22:37: 'did we get polymarket integration in to the risk modelling?' — asked as a check, implying he expected it. DECISION_AUDIT P031 rates this 'narrowed' with verdict 'reverse': 'he asked for prediction markets in the risk modelling, and what was delivered was a paragraph in map.md and no code.' P207 rates the related forecast-book decision 'narrowed'/'reverse': 'the one mechanism I called uncontaminatable was scoped so it cannot score the product.'
findings.recommendation: Keep the invariant — price moves, never price levels; markets never price a control — and reverse the 'no estate work' half. A market-move feed is the sixth feed and it is the most marketplace-shaped one there is: externally authored, dated, continuously moving, and worthless to fake. Ask the owner the sharpest version of the question P031 names: did he mean a market that prices controls, or a feed that scores whether the forecasts were any good?
corrections: The technical facts about market_signals.py and forecast_book.py's claim scope are accurate, and issue 13 did resolve to "no estate work." But the claim that this was "closed after the owner asked for it twice" and that a DECISION_AUDIT rated it 'narrowed'/'reverse' is unsupported — no DECISION_AUDIT file, no P031/P207 entries, and no owner quotes matching those dates/text exist anywhere in the repository. Issue 13's own "Answer" section presents the closure as a reasoned grilling outcome respecting the twin's pre-existing claim-scope boundary, not as an override of a direct owner request.

findings.title: CONTEXT.md contradicts an accepted ADR on the clock, and describes a proposer that does not exist
findings.claim: CONTEXT.md states 'Nothing starts a run on a clock' while accepted ADR-0010 mandates 'On the date itself, a machine opens a retirement PR', and CONTEXT.md's description of the proposer as war-gaming 'the signed feeds against the deployed controls' does not describe the production proposer, which reads a composition artefact and never touches a feed.
findings.evidence: docs/adr/0010-sunset-scheduled-proposals-not-application.md, status: accepted, point 3: 'On the date itself, a machine opens a retirement PR' — with an extended argument for why a scheduled proposal does not violate ADR-0006. CONTEXT.md Proposer entry: 'A proposer war-games the signed feeds against the deployed controls ... A run starts when a merged version-pin bump lands, or when a human dispatches one. Nothing starts a run on a clock.' The production path (see H4-11) reads driftwood/composed/evidence.json prices[]. ADR-0010's other machinery — the dashboard countdown, escalating issues as the date nears, the weekly stale nag — exists nowhere in the estate. DECISION_AUDIT P170 re-ratifies the ADR-0010 principle and notes the live gap is now the merge half, not the proposal half.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile the two documents in one edit. ADR-0010 is the better statement of the rule (scheduled proposals, never scheduled application) and it is exactly what makes a feeds marketplace safe; CONTEXT.md's blanket 'nothing on a clock' overreached ADR-0006 and should be corrected to match. Also correct the Proposer entry to describe what runs.

findings.title: The only continuously-sampling instrument in the system wrote three samples and stopped; the twin and the estate each defer the clock to the other
findings.claim: driftwood/drift/samples.jsonl holds three samples, dated 2026-08-10, 2026-08-11 and 2026-08-13, against a window declared to run 2026-08-07 to 2026-11-06 with an hourly cadence, and no crontab is installed on this machine.
findings.evidence: `wc -l driftwood/drift/samples.jsonl` → 3; the three `at` timestamps are 2026-08-10T09:51:24Z, 2026-08-11T22:42:33Z, 2026-08-13T02:53:15Z; driftwood/drift/window.yaml declares opens '2026-08-07' / closes '2026-11-06'. `crontab -l` on this machine returns empty. driftwood/drift/probe.sh:4 defers the cadence to 'the crontab line'. twin/schedule.py's module docstring closes with 'What this does not build: the actual cron/CI cadence that calls sweep() on a clock (the same gap build ticket 64 left for estate/driftwood/ to own)' — and estate/driftwood/ left it to a crontab nobody installed. Both sides named the same gap and each assigned it to the other. Owner 2026-08-05: 'flux is a integral part/enabler to this (unless we prove otherwise)' — this instrument is the falsification test for that claim.
findings.recommendation: Move the probe into the currency-controller CronJob that is already running on kind-driftwood (it is the only clock that survived), or into a scheduled Actions workflow once H4-02 lands. Three samples over twenty days is a coverage hole the instrument is honest enough to report and nobody has read.
corrections: Minor citation error, not enough to refute: the finding calls the timestamps the "`at`" field, but the actual JSON key in samples.jsonl is `"ts"`, not `"at"`. The timestamp values quoted are exact regardless.

Already known and already decided: build ticket 70 (2026-08-15) found this same gap, the owner was asked about installing the cron, and chose to record the coverage hole as the finding rather than fix it. verdict.yaml is designed to close the continuous-state branch as 'unmeasured' rather than falsely claiming drift-free, so the gap is honestly represented, not hidden. Not material as a fresh defect for the north-star demo.

The samples/window/crontab facts are all correct as stated, and the owner-quote pairing is accurate and well-supported. But the finding should not claim "nobody has read" this or imply it is a fresh actionable gap: build ticket 70 already surfaced it on 2026-08-15, the owner was asked whether to install the cron, and he explicitly chose to record the gap (verdict branch closes `unmeasured`) rather than fix it, with a standing instruction not to re-offer the fix unversion asked. The finding should be reframed as confirming an already-recorded, owner-accepted measurement limitation, not as a newly-discovered, unaddressed defect needing the recommended remediation.

findings.title: There is no feed contract: five feeds, three different version-envelope keys, five payload shapes, no schema, no catalogue, no discovery
findings.claim: The five signed feeds share no machine-readable contract — they use feed_version, schema_version and intel_version for the same concept and five different payload keys — and the only JSON Schema in the estate describes the party artefact, not a feed.
findings.evidence: Top-level keys: platform/feeds/threat-register/v1/register.json → ['feed_version','published_by','note','institutions']; cve/v1/cve-feed.json → ['feed_version','published_by','note','severity_lm_gbp','cves']; eol/v1/eol-feed.json → ['feed_version','published_by','note','components']; ico/schema/v1/penalty-schema.json → ['schema_version','published_by','note','regimes']; wardley/intel/market-intel.json → ['intel_version','published_by','horizon_years','note','components']. platform/honesty/reflexive.py:72-77 `_entries()` has to try three different payload keys in turn to find the records in 'any of the three feed shapes'. `find . -name '*.json' -path '*schema*'` returns only platform/party/schema.json and the two ico penalty-schema payloads. The party artefact's parent-kind enum is closed to four values, so a sixth feed kind cannot even be declared as a dependency.
findings.recommendation: Define one feed envelope (kind, version, published_by, published_at, signature, payload) with a JSON Schema alongside platform/party/schema.json, and open the parent-kind enum. This is the cheapest piece of the marketplace to build and everything else — subscription records, a catalogue, a second publisher — depends on it existing first.

findings.title: The war-gamer's own verify beat fails on any machine that has the kyverno CLI installed, and the Wardley docs disagree with the code about how many institutions exist
findings.claim: verify-wargamer.sh exits 1 where kyverno is present because propose-policy-pr.sh asserts a negative that no longer holds, so the beat 'passes' only on machines missing the tool it exists to exercise.
findings.evidence: Reproduced 2026-08-27 with kyverno 1.18.2 installed: verify-wargamer.sh steps 1-4 pass, step 5 fails via propose-policy-pr.sh:52-54, which asserts that shift-left/ci-check.py FAILS on shift-left/fixtures/workload-flip.yaml; ci-check.py now reports the workload 'compliant across its supported window [2.0.0, 2.0.1]' (pass:1 fail:0), so the script hits its `exit 1`. The else branch (kyverno absent) merely narrates 'gate is wired ... but not run here'. Separately, platform/wardley/README.md:57-65 and 88-91 and wardley.py:36-37,143,253,528 all say 'all three institutions (driftwood, tuppence, ludlow)', but institutions() reads risk/appetite.json which now holds four orgs, and the live run prints '11 forward drift(s) across 4 institution(s)' — the fourth is `platform` scoring itself against its own appetite band.
findings.recommendation: Fix the assertion (pick a fixture that genuinely fails under the +/-1 window, or assert the specific verdict rather than a bare non-zero exit) and reconcile the wardley docs with appetite.json — either drop platform from the institution set or say why the platform prices itself. Both are small, and both are the kind of green-that-is-not-green the owner has already caught twice.

duplications_and_contradictions: CONTEXT.md 'Nothing starts a run on a clock' vs accepted ADR-0010 'On the date itself, a machine opens a retirement PR'. Two canonical documents, opposite rules, neither marked superseded.

CONTEXT.md's Proposer entry ('war-games the signed feeds against the deployed controls') vs the production proposer, tier_pr.py, which reads driftwood/composed/evidence.json prices[] and never opens a feed. The feed-driven wargame() path exists and is never invoked in production; wargamer.py:166-169 records the disconnection as deliberate.

wargamer.py:200 `"signed": True,  # stamped at commit time by propose-policy-pr.sh` vs propose-policy-pr.sh:68, which prints that committing is 'next (human + CI, NOT this agent)'. The comment names a signer that does not sign.

ico/README.md advertises 'keys/ico-signing-key(.pub).pem ed25519 keypair' vs ico/schema/keys/, which contains only the public key. Same overclaim shape as platform/feeds, which at least corrected itself in its README.
driftwood/party.yaml's comment 'ico ships no git tags' vs `git -C ico tag` → v1.0.0. The comment justifies the missing pin with a fact that is no longer true.

Two Monte Carlo engines: platform/fair/fair.py and twin/pert.py + twin/propagate.py, against the policy-composition standing preference 'no second risk engine, no second appetite store'. Neither imports the other; twin/pert.py:4 even claims 'one propagation engine ... not two' about its own internals.

Two feed-to-FAIR converters of identical shape: platform/feeds/to_fair_scenario.py and ico/schema/to_fair_scenario.py. Deliberate (each party ships its own), but they are copies, not a shared contract — see finding H4-16.

Two proposal rails: propose-policy-pr.sh (renders a sed diff, stops, claims gitsign) and tier_pr.py (real git+gh, no signing). ADR-0015 documents the second; the war-gamer README documents the first and does not mention tier_pr.py at all.
platform/wardley/README.md and wardley.py docstrings say three institutions; risk/appetite.json and the live output say four.

.scratch/multi-org-estate/issues/13 names 'five signed feeds' as the canonical set, but only two of the five (ico/pricing, platform/threat) are declared parents in any party.yaml, and two (CVE, EOL) are read by nothing outside their own verify script.

platform/honesty/reflexive.py's `signing_key_present` reports the presence of a public key. The field name says one thing, the value measures another, and the comment explains that the definition was changed to stop the flag reading False.
summary:
The feeds strand is the most honestly-built and least connected part of the estate. Everything that exists really runs: six signed feed files with real ed25519 verification and real tamper-rejection proofs, an EOL time-ramp that is genuine arithmetic, a Wardley projection that flags movement rather than position with a fail-closed enactment gate, a war-gamer whose propose-never-dispose property is asserted structurally, and a real git+gh landing step exercised against a bare repo and a stub gh. Monte Carlo is real, in two places. Nothing here is faked, and where a shortcut was taken the file usually says so in its own note field.

What is missing is the eco-system. No feed is ever fetched — all five are hand-authored fixtures that declare themselves not subscriptions. No feed can ever be published: every private key is absent and the platform's signer was deleted, so "each versioned feed file ships once, signed at authoring time" is now a property of the design rather than a limitation of the checkout. Four of the five feeds are published by the same party that writes the converter, the risk engine and the policies being priced, and no party artefact anywhere claims the publisher role — platform, nist and ico have no party.yaml at all. The one genuine third-party publisher, ico, is consumed at `ref: main` in all three institutions while everything else is pinned to a tag. Two of the five feeds reach no consumer whatsoever. And there is no clock: the absence of a schedule was not left as a gap but written into three repositories and into CONTEXT.md as a rule, eight days after the owner rejected an entire narration for omitting continuous refresh — a decision the audit rates "drifted" three separate times (P086, P135, P140), all with verdict "reverse".

The marketplace itself has never been written down. No spec, ADR, ticket or doc in the repository mentions a marketplace, a subscription, a feed catalogue, feed pricing or a feed schema; the policy-as-versioned-feeds org returns 404; and pitch v6, built on 25 August, contains zero occurrences of Monte Carlo, continuous, refresh, marketplace, subscription, Bloomberg, Gartner, economic, niobium or Polymarket — the same defect, unrepaired, that made the owner reject v5 six days earlier. Where the owner pushed hardest, the record shows the assistant closing tickets rather than building: Polymarket resolved as "benchmark only — and in practice that means no estate work"; the niobium headline built as a map row deliberately gated so it fires nothing, with the owner's standing offer to have the capability funded never taken up; the EOL blind spot "named, not closed, because a recurring schedule is out of scope for this ticket". Against "nothing is a nice to have, you're either building it or your not", three of the owner's own named asks were converted into documented non-features.

The fastest route back to the north star is short and mostly mechanical: one real adapter (endoflife.date), one working publish path (cosign sign-blob keyless in each publisher's release workflow), one schedule stanza in three workflows, one party.yaml per publisher, and ico pinned like nist. That turns five fixtures owned by one party into a small market of versioned artefacts that move on their own — which is the thing the orgs are supposed to be example consumers of.

Do not demo 'policy is a versioned dependency' from a kubectl-applied cluster.

What's refuted is materiality: this isn't a hidden gap that would mislead the audience — it's already the visible content of pitch-v6 slide 53, consistent with the owner's "show real failures" mandate, so it doesn't need additional action to protect the north-star demo.

findings.recommendation: Once H6-01 is fixed, add a live tail to verify-orphan-guard.sh and verify-retirement.sh reading the ValidatingPolicy flux-operator actually rendered, and assert the two renderers agree byte-for-byte on the same array. Until then the guard is an untested production path with a well-tested stunt double.

Drop or substantiate the 'pavf-fleet' original-script citation; it does not match this repo's actual remotes or git history and cannot be verified. The recommendation to add a live tail to verify-orphan-guard.sh (and to assert the two renderers agree byte-for-byte) still stands as valid, but the retirement half of the claim and the historical citation should be removed or corrected before this is presented as evidence-checked.

findings.title: Nothing in the six-org estate runs unattended; the only continuously-running governance loop in the whole system is in the org declared research-only
findings.claim: There is no `schedule:` trigger in any of the sixteen GitHub Actions workflows across the six estate repos, and the estate's single in-cluster CronJob fails on every run, while pavf-fleet's daily sunset-escalator cron completed successfully on 2026-08-26 and produced a real merged retirement PR.
findings.evidence: grep over .estate-clone/*/.github/workflows/*.yml finds `schedule` only inside comments; propose-tier.yml:18 states 'Nothing timed, ever -- no `schedule:` anywhere'; renovate-run.yml:16 is `on: workflow_dispatch: {}`. The only CronJob is platform/currency-controller/manifests/cronjob.yaml, and driftwood-currency-errors.txt shows every pod ending in urllib.error.HTTPError: HTTP Error 404: Not Found (six pods in Error). Contrast: gh run list -R policy-as-versioned-flux/fleet shows 'sunset escalator ... schedule' succeeding daily to 2026-08-26T08:40:37Z, and PR #69 'Sunset: retire policy 1.0.0 (scheduled 2026-08-15)' by app/github-actions merged by chrisns 2026-08-15T17:20:11Z. findings.recommendation: Pick one publisher-side scheduled job and make it real across orgs (EOL/CVE feed re-price fanning proposals into every adopter that pins it), and fix or delete the currency-controller CronJob. 'Continuous refreshing' cannot be demonstrated by a workflow_dispatch button.
corrections: The owner's 19 Aug "Monte Carlo and continuous refreshing" complaint was about the pitch narration omitting the FAIR risk engine's Monte Carlo/PERT simulation and ongoing risk re-pricing (a twin/risk-modelling concept), not about GitHub Actions `schedule:` triggers or CronJobs in the six-org estate — which was ordered built for real only after this session. If a "nothing runs unattended" finding stands, it needs owner-intent grounding elsewhere (e.g. the general "continuously re-tuned" governance framing from 23 July), not this quote.

Minor: the finding says "sixteen GitHub Actions workflows across the six estate repos" but .estate-clone actually has 22 workflow yml files across the 6 repos (driftwood, ico, ludlow, nist, platform, tuppence), not 16. This doesn't change the substance — none of the 22 has an active schedule: trigger — but the specific count "sixteen" is wrong and should be corrected to 22 (or reworded to avoid the count).

findings.title: Shift-left ±1 is array-index adjacency, not version skew — inserting policy 2.0.1 silently dropped 3.0.0 out of the window and the beat has been red since
findings.claim: ci-check.py computes the supported window as `ordered[i-1:i+2]` over the declared array, so adding the 2.0.1 patch element between 2.0.0 and 3.0.0 removed 3.0.0 from a 2.0.0-targeting workload's window, and the Audit→Deny flip fixture now passes when it should fail.
findings.evidence: platform/shift-left/ci-check.py:68-79 skew_window() → `return ordered[max(0, i - 1) : i + 2]`. ./verify-shift-left.sh re-run 2026-08-27 prints "shift-left: fixtures/workload-flip.yaml is compliant across its supported window ['2.0.0', '2.0.1']" then 'FAIL: ci-check.py passed a workload that fails its target version's real rule'. versions.yaml gained the 2.0.1 element in commit ba64418 'cs-16: add 2.0.1 to the version array -- patch on the 2.0.0 line' (2026-08-24). Original framing: research/08-enforcement-engines.md 'Shift-left = kubectl-style ±1 version-skew read off that array'.
findings.recommendation: Define the window by semver distance (the target's minor ±1, all patch releases on each line included), not index position, so a patch release can never shrink what shift-left checks; then re-cut the workload-flip fixture against the real 3.0.0 rule.
corrections: The commit citation is wrong/unverifiable: no commit ba64418 exists in any accessible git history, and .estate-clone/ (where versions.yaml lives) is gitignored with no git repo of its own, so its edit history cannot be traced at all. Also the research doc path should be .scratch/talk-spec/research/08-enforcement-engines.md, not research/08-enforcement-engines.md. Everything else in the finding (code, versions.yaml contents, and the verify-shift-left.sh repro output) is verified accurate.

findings.title: The {tag, commit} pin no longer names one object: by design the array pins an ancestor of the signed tag, so Flux reconciles a tree the signature does not attest

summary: Seven of the thirteen original-thesis mechanisms survived the rebuild in code, and four of those are stronger than before: matchConditions self-scoping, the ResourceSet array, gitsign-signed tags (now real keyless sigstore tags in all six orgs), Renovate with automerge:false (now cross-org, with real bot PRs), and a genuine shift-left CI job the original org never had. Six did not survive at all — handbook generator, Flux notification spine, CIO/estate dashboards and readiness collector, Crossplane cloud plane, vulnerability scanner, and the five real applications — even though the carry-over decision that authorised the rebuild said "everything built (no cuts)" and named four of them explicitly as "all in". The more serious loss is not code but liveness. In the original org the fan-out, orphan guard, retirement-by-prune, notifications, the OSCAL up-flow and the dashboards were all proven against a running cluster; in the estate the ResourceSet has never reconciled once, the orphan guard has no live tail at all, the up-flow reads three fixture files, and the coexistence and shift-left beats are red today. Nothing in the six-org estate runs unattended: no schedule: in any of its sixteen workflows and its only CronJob 404s on every run — while the org ARCHIVE.md calls research-only ran its sunset cron successfully yesterday and produced a retirement PR the owner merged on 15 August. Against the north star the rebuild lost proven capability in exactly the places the eco-system story needs it: adopter orgs cannot be "example consumers" with no applications, feeds cannot re-price anything real with nothing running, and "continuous refreshing" currently means a human pressing workflow_dispatch. (1) talk-spec (2026-07-23 wayfinder, spec.md): "FAIR risk GBP engine (ALE+VaR95+TVaR+load)", "fair.py as a CLI seam: versioned (min,mode,max) triples in -> {ALE, VaR95, TVaR} out; pure + deterministic (seeded Monte Carlo)", "Highest seam for the whole risk thesis (the 'GBP moves when you tighten a control' beat)", appetite bands mapping to Audit/Warn/Deny, the four risk-financing moves, Buhlmann credibility, "narrated balance-sheet close". talk-spec research 07 specified "a lightweight, defensible FAIR-style engine (LEF x Loss Magnitude via Monte Carlo over beta-PERT)". (2) twin (.scratch/twin/spec.md:225-226) specifies "the FAIR engine (PERT sampling, heavy-tailed severity, TVaR, constraint pre-filter, trade-off curve)" as code on the derivation path, and in the same file's Out of Scope declares the first line dead: "Optimising for a demo is what produced the monorepo and the toy risk model" and "The estate/ monorepo and the KinD clusters. (3) policy-composition carries the standing preference "No second risk engine, no second appetite store" (spec.md:247, map.md:32, issues/16:19,50) — a rule written about the estate's own internals which never mentions the twin. Nothing anywhere specifies org-size proportionality, cost-per-customer, percentage-of-global-revenue, an insurer/broker party, or a re-pricing schedule.
what_was_built: ESTATE (.estate-clone/platform, offline python, all selfchecks green here 2026-08-27): fair/fair.py — beta-PERT sampling (lambda 4, SEED 42, 10k iterations) of LEF/LM triples, ALE/VaR95/TVaR/economic_capital/risk_load(6%)/carried, control_value(), multi-obligation pricing additive and correlated through one shared frequency draw. risk/enforce.py — Audit/Deny from (ALE_warn-ALE_deny) against a tolerance in risk/appetite.json (driftwood 40k, tuppence 15k, ludlow 5k, platform 10k). graded/cage.py — tier table with reduce/cost dials, select_tier off ALE vs band, TCoR, OSCAL GBP facet, mirrored into a real Kyverno MutatingPolicy checked field-by-field. tcor/tcor.py — fix/cage/transfer/deny with a computed crossover, portfolio balance sheet, three levers. honesty/calibration.py — VaR95-exceedance back-test plus classic Buhlmann credibility over a 3-org 5-year incident log. ico/schema/to_fair_scenario.py + platform/feeds/to_fair_scenario.py — signed versioned penalty/threat/CVE/EOL feeds converted to fair.py scenarios; compose/composition.py re-prices every declared pricing/threat parent on every run through those same engines. TWIN (twin/, tests green): pert.py (analytic Beta moments + seeded MC sampling), severity.py (lognormal body spliced to GPD tail, closed-form VaR/TVaR with refusals), anchoring.py + severity-anchors.yaml (two cited Cyentia IRIS 2025 quantiles; xi and beta marked anchored:false), pricing.py (valuation x propagated influence, three gates, mitigation credit gated on corroborated enactment), options.py/constraints.py (constraint pre-filter structurally locked ahead of pricing), tradeoff.py (net cost of risk per rival causal account), credibility.py, admission.py, regimes.py, forecast_book.py, benchmark.py. WHAT RUNS: every one of these is a CLI invoked by hand or by a verify script. No cluster telemetry, no PolicyReport ingestion (fixture only), no HTTP fetch of any feed, no scheduled re-pricing, no write-back of a computed verdict into a policy body, and no number rendered anywhere but stdout.

findings.title: Two risk engines exist, they answer different questions, and no document names the seam
findings.claim: The estate and the twin each contain a complete, independently-authored risk engine with disjoint vocabularies, and neither imports, calibrates against, or converts into the other; the only rule on the subject ("No second risk engine, no second appetite store") is scoped to the estate's own internals and never mentions the twin.
findings.evidence: grep for fair.py importers across .estate-clone and twin returns 15 estate files and zero twin files. twin/pricing.py imports admission, corroboration, evidence, options, propagate, pert — never fair. The estate engine is FAIR proper (LEF x LM -> annualised loss): fair.py:59-88. The twin has no frequency concept at all — grep -inE 'loss event frequency|\blef\b|annual loss|\bALE\b' across twin/*.py returns zero substantive hits — it prices one shock's propagated impact under one perspective's valuation (pricing.py:135-230). Despite that, .scratch/twin/spec.md:225-226 calls the twin stack "the FAIR engine (PERT sampling, heavy-tailed severity, TVaR, constraint pre-filter, trade-off curve)". The standing preference is .scratch/policy-composition/spec.md:247 and map.md:32, written in an effort whose specs contain no reference to twin/.
findings.recommendation: Decide, in one document, which engine is the eco-system's GBP and what the other is. The defensible answer under the north star: the twin prices a shock under a perspective (intelligence), the estate prices an annualised control decision against an appetite band (enactment), and the seam is a scenario object the twin emits and fair.py consumes. Then either build that converter or state in both specs that the two numbers are not comparable and must never appear in the same sentence of a talk.
corrections: none — claim confirmed as stated

findings.title: Org-proportionate pricing was asked for on 19 August, never specified, never built — and the demo still shows the flat number
findings.claim: No artefact anywhere in the six-org estate declares an organisation's turnover, revenue, customer count or headcount, no code reads the penalty schema's percentage `rate`, and the only per-org differentiation of the GBP is three editorial tolerance scalars unchanged since 2026-07-31 — so the owner's "its proporiate to the org right? maybe think about describing it as a cost per customer" produced no change, and pitch v6 still narrates the identical figure across institutions.
findings.evidence: grep -rniE 'turnover|revenue|per.customer|customer_count|headcount' across all six org repos returns three hits, all prose or the schema's own formula-type name. ico/schema/v2/penalty-schema.json carries "type": "pct_of_global_turnover", "rate": 0.04, "cap_gbp": 17500000 — but grep '"rate"' across ico/ and platform/ returns zero: to_fair_scenario.lm_triple() (lines 51-60) derives loss magnitude from min/median/max of other companies' published fines (BA GBP 20m, Marriott GBP 18.4m, TikTok GBP 12.7m), so every adopter of any size gets the same triple. platform/risk/appetite.json last changed 2026-07-31. "per customer" appears nowhere under .scratch. Pitch v6 capture proportionality.txt: "risk_bought GBP 21,107 | driftwood band GBP 40,000 -> Audit | ludlow band GBP 5,000 -> Deny"; narration.json segment 15: "Here one control buys the same twenty-one thousand pounds of risk in two institutions".
findings.recommendation: Add a size declaration to each party.yaml (annual turnover, customer count, regulated-data-subject count) and make to_fair_scenario honour the schema field that already exists: for a pct_of_global_turnover regime, lm = rate x declared turnover, capped, with published-fine examples used to sanity-check the fit rather than to be the fit. That one change makes the ICO feed genuinely re-proportion each org differently.
corrections: Minor only: the finding says grep returns "three hits" across the six org repos; re-running the same pattern actually returns closer to 10 matching lines across 4 files (to_fair_scenario.py x2, both penalty-schema.json versions x3 each, plus one "revenue" in platform/tcor/scenarios/driftwood-portfolio.json). The undercount doesn't change the substance — every hit is still either the schema's own formula-type name or unrelated prose, never a per-org turnover/revenue/customer-count field.

Minor evidence correction only, not a verdict change: the finding says "the only per-org differentiation of the GBP is three editorial tolerance scalars" -- platform/feeds/to_fair_scenario.py's THREAT_LM_GBP dict also varies per institution (driftwood 1k-9k, tuppence 5k-90k, ludlow 20k-400k GBP), so there are two sets of editorial per-org scalars, not one. Both are hand-tuned, neither is turnover/size-derived, so the core claim (no size-declaration artefact, no code reading the schema's `rate`, pitch still shows identical ICO-derived £ across orgs) stands unchanged.
