findings.title: The back-test narrates the flattering org and omits a 40% VaR95 exceedance rate on the other
findings.claim: The same calibration run that produces the narrated "over-prices the health provider by roughly eight times, with no breaches of its own confidence bound" also reports driftwood breaching its own VaR95 in 2 of 5 years — a 40% exceedance rate against 5% expected — and the narration mentions only the first.
findings.evidence: Run here 2026-08-27, `python3 platform/honesty/calibration.py backtest`: driftwood model_ale 19,559 vs observed 35,000, exceedances 2/5, exceedance_rate 0.4, verdict "under-prices (too many VaR95 breaches) — recalibrate up"; ludlow model_ale 1,025,511 vs observed 130,000, exceedances 0/5, verdict "over-prices". narration.json segment 45 and deck.html:519 carry only the ludlow line. Separately, "no breaches of its own confidence bound" carries no evidential weight at n=5 (expected 0.25); calibration.py:135-137 says so itself — "a binomial with n<10 is too small for Kupiec".
findings.recommendation: Narrate both verdicts in one breath — "it under-prices the retailer and over-prices the health provider, and it says so" — which is a stronger honesty claim than the current one, and drop the "no breaches of its own confidence bound" clause, which the code's own comment disowns.

findings.title: The back-test compares a single privileged operation's exposure against an organisation's whole loss history
findings.claim: incidents.json points ludlow and tuppence at break-glass access-exposure scenarios that model the cost of one privileged operation going wrong, then compares each scenario's annualised warn-state loss to that organisation's entire five-year annual loss record and pools all three orgs as equal-exposure risks in one Buhlmann portfolio — so the 7.9x figure measures a category mismatch, not the model.
findings.evidence: incidents.json maps ludlow -> ../break-glass/scenarios/ludlow-patient-data.json, whose note reads "the GBP EXPOSURE of doing this op wrongly / from the wrong hands" (a single emergency read of a patient record, lm 50k/200k/2m), and tuppence -> break-glass/scenarios/tuppence-write.json ("A mutating op on bank account state"), while driftwood maps to fair/scenarios/driftwood-cart-pii.json, a workload-level PII risk. calibration.backtest_org() (calibration.py:99-146) takes each scenario's warn-state ALE as the model prediction for that org's annual losses; buhlmann() (calibration.py:68-95) documents its own input as "a portfolio of equal-exposure risks".
findings.recommendation: Back-test like against like: give each org one portfolio-level scenario (or sum its per-risk scenarios) and compare that to its annual loss history, keeping the break-glass scenarios for the access-tier decision they were built for. Until then the 7.9x number should not appear on a slide.
corrections: n/a — finding stands as written

findings.title: Nothing consumes the recalibration the honesty layer computes
findings.claim: calibration.py emits a recalibration_factor per org (driftwood 2.11, i.e. the model under-prices by more than double) and no code in the estate reads it; no scenario triple or appetite band has changed since, so a known mis-calibration has stood for over a month with no route from the finding to the number.
findings.evidence: grep for recalibration_factor across .estate-clone returns only calibration.py itself and two prose lines in verify-honesty.sh. `calibration.py recalibrate` run here: driftwood recalibration_factor 2.108, tuppence 1.175. git log: platform/risk/appetite.json unchanged since 2026-07-31; fair/ last touched 2026-08-20 for multi-obligation pricing, not recalibration. honesty/README.md:134-139 defers "the signed recalibration PR that a moved GBP would open".
findings.recommendation: Close the loop cheaply: have the honesty run write the recalibration factor into a versioned calibration feed under platform/feeds/, which to_fair_scenario already converts and composition already re-prices against. Recalibration then becomes a signed dependency bump — a mechanism the estate already has.
corrections: The recalibration_factor is indeed uncomsumed (confirmed by grep), but the estate already discloses this in README.md:134-139 as a deliberate, uniform limitation of the propose-never-dispose pattern rather than a surprising unclosed loop — so it's not material to demonstrating the north star as a fresh finding.

Reframe as expected/documented scope (matches "propose, never dispose" and the README's own "Not stood up here" list), not an unaddressed major drift against owner intent — at most a minor/documentation-adjacent note that the deferred step could be made more discoverable, not a severity-major gap.

One evidence claim is imprecise, not wrong in substance: platform/risk/appetite.json was NOT literally "unchanged since 2026-07-31" — it was touched again on 2026-08-20 (commit "Add a machine-checked roles: declaration per party"). However that touch only added a new `platform` org entry and reworded the note; the actual driftwood/tuppence/ludlow tolerance numbers (40000/15000/5000) that the recalibration factor would need to move are indeed unchanged since the 2026-07-31 wave build. The core claim — no recalibration has been applied to the appetite band or scenario pricing since the honesty layer computed the factor — still holds.

findings.title: "Continuous refreshing" is not built, and the estate is deliberately built so it cannot be
findings.claim: Nothing in the estate re-prices anything on a schedule, by design: the enforcement decision asserts no clock can reach it, the proposer workflow states it has no schedule, and the only time-varying risk input is a ramp driven by a human-supplied --as-of argument — so the owner's 2026-08-19 constraint that Monte Carlo and continuous refreshing be present is half met.
findings.evidence: risk/enforce.py:109-115 — selfcheck asserts no datetime/time import can leak into the decision path. driftwood/.github/workflows/propose-tier.yml:18 — "Nothing timed, ever -- no `schedule:` anywhere"; triggers are a merged pin bump or manual dispatch. policy-composition issues/16 AC — "The composition calls no scheduler and reads no wall clock except through an explicit --as-of argument". The only cron in the estate (platform/currency-controller/manifests/cronjob.yaml, every minute) reconciles policy-version currency, not price. platform/feeds/to_fair_scenario.eol_ramp() is the sole time-varying input and takes as_of as an argument. The Monte Carlo half is genuinely built (fair.py:49-88, twin/pert.py:177-225, twin/propagate.py:239-304).
findings.recommendation: Separate the two things ADR-0006 conflates. Time-conditional policy bodies stay banned. A scheduled re-pricing that opens a PR when the number crosses a band is not time-conditional policy — it is ADR-0010's "timed nudge to a human". One scheduled workflow re-running composition's price step and opening the tier PR is the whole of "continuous refreshing" the owner asked for.

findings.title: No feed is fetched from anywhere; the feeds marketplace is a signing convention
findings.claim: Every risk input in the estate is a hand-authored JSON file committed in the same project that consumes it — no HTTP call exists in any converter, no publisher exists outside the six repos, and the platform authors the threat register that prices its own adopters.
findings.evidence: grep for curl/requests/urllib/https in platform/feeds/*.py, platform/feeds/*.sh, ico/schema/*.py and ico/*.sh returns only gitsign certificate-identity regexes, no fetch. Feed notes self-describe: "trivy/GHSA-style CVE feed", "endoflife.date-style feed", "institution threat register ... editorial". platform/feeds/to_fair_scenario.py:33-38 hardcodes THREAT_LM_GBP for driftwood/tuppence/ludlow in the platform's own source. driftwood/party.yaml inherits "{ party: platform, kind: threat, version: v1 }" and its own header notes that pricing and threat "have no Flux pin anywhere in this estate today".
findings.recommendation: One real fetch changes the claim entirely: pull endoflife.date (public, unauthenticated, stable JSON) into the eol feed on a scheduled workflow that commits a new signed version. That makes one of three feeds genuinely external and gives the schedule from H3-07 something real to carry.

findings.title: Every tail measure the engine computes is decoration — every decision is made on the mean
findings.claim: fair.py computes VaR95, TVaR, economic capital, a Solvency-II 6% risk load and a "carried" figure, and no decision in the estate reads any of them: enforcement, cage-tier selection, TCoR and the insurance premium all read ALE only, and the sole reader of var95 is the back-test.
findings.evidence: grep for tvar|carried|var95|economic_capital|risk_load across .estate-clone/**/*.py excluding fair.py returns only honesty/calibration.py (var95, for exceedance counting) and unrelated string matches. risk/enforce.py decides on (ALE_warn - ALE_deny). graded/cage.py:138 — `uncaged = fair.summarize(...)["ale"]`. tcor/tcor.py:66-67,84-87 — every move priced from _ale(); tcor.py:111 prices the insurance premium as `ale_warn * (1.0 + load)`, with tcor.py:57-61 conceding the 0.40 load is "a documented mid-range guess, not a quoted rate".
findings.recommendation: Make one decision tail-driven and the apparatus earns its keep: price the transfer move off TVaR between an attachment point and a limit rather than off ALE, and set the cage's deny rung on economic capital rather than residual mean. Otherwise delete the unused outputs.
corrections: The claim "no decision in the estate reads any of them" and "cage-tier selection ... read ALE only" is wrong: platform/break-glass/break-glass.py (ticket 19) sets its assurance tier and CAGE/DENY/STEP_UP/ALLOW decision entirely from `carried` (TVaR + risk load) via `carried_gbp()`/`required_tier()`, is documented and cross-referenced from other README files, and its selfcheck runs and passes. The grep claim that other tail-measure references are "only honesty/calibration.py ... and unrelated string matches" is also incomplete — it misses this file. fair.py's other cited numbers (var95/tvar/economic_capital/risk_load/carried definitions, enforce.py's ALE-only gate, cage.py:138, tcor.py's ALE-based pricing and 0.40 load comment) are accurate as far as they go, but the overall "decoration, nothing reads the tail" thesis does not hold.

The claim "no decision in the estate reads any of them ... the sole reader of var95 is the back-test" is false: platform/break-glass/break-glass.py's decide()/required_tier() reads fair.py's `carried` (TVaR + risk_load) to set the assurance tier (and CAGE/DENY rung) for break-glass access — a real, wired decision driven by a tail measure, not ALE. The finding should be narrowed to "TCoR, cage.py's routine graded-enforcement tier, and the insurance premium calc read ALE only" (which does appear accurate for tcor.py/cage.py/enforce.py) rather than the blanket claim that nothing but the back-test reads the tail outputs.

graded/cage.py:138 does read ale-only for its own tiering (that part of the claim holds), and var95 specifically is only read by honesty/calibration.py's back-test — but the broader headline ('every decision is made on the mean', 'no decision... reads any of them') is false: platform/break-glass/break-glass.py's access-tier/CAGE decision is driven by TVaR+risk_load (carried), fulfilling the finding's own recommended fix already.

findings.title: The engine that drives every enforcement decision has a bounded light tail, which is the property the twin's own spec used to reject a rival technology
findings.claim: fair.simulate() draws frequency from a bounded beta-PERT and rounds it, and each event's magnitude from a bounded beta-PERT, so annual loss is hard-bounded at (max LEF x max LM) and cannot express a ruin-class event — while the twin built a GPD tail precisely because that is a lie, and twin/spec.md rejected Google TabFM for having "no PERT triples, no GPD tail, no TVaR".
findings.evidence: fair.py:49-56 (pert on a closed [lo,hi] interval), :78-88 (freqs = rounded PERT draws; per-year loss is a sum of PERT draws) — nothing can exceed max_lef x max_lm. twin/severity.py:81-175 — lognormal body spliced to a GPD tail with closed-form TVaR and a refusal at xi>=1. .scratch/twin/spec.md:420 — TabFM rejected because it is "architecturally incapable of a predictive distribution — no PERT triples, no GPD tail, no TVaR — and the shipped pipeline clips at +/-4 sigma, amputating exactly the heavy tail the risk engine exists to measure". pitch-v6 narration segment 73 makes the heavy-tail argument out loud about the twin, immediately after forty minutes of estate beats priced by the bounded engine.
findings.recommendation: Either give fair.py a tail — twin/severity.py is 215 lines of tested code taking a triple-shaped input, so splicing it in as an optional LM model is a small diff — or say plainly that the estate's number is a mean-of-bounded-losses for control comparison and that ruin-class exposure lives in the twin. Do not make the heavy-tail argument on stage forty minutes after showing numbers that cannot express one.
corrections: One evidence detail is imprecise, not the core claim: the finding says the heavy-tail argument (segment 73) lands "forty minutes" after the bounded-engine £ beats — the actual pitch is ~20:08 total (per project memory) and the relevant fair.py beats sit around segments 39-47 (~10-12 min in) with segment 74 at ~18 min, so the gap is closer to 6-8 minutes, not forty. The substantive claim — bounded engine's numbers precede an unacknowledged heavy-tail argument in the same talk, and both derive from the same TabFM-rejection logic — holds regardless.

The architecture/spec/code claims are all accurate and should stand. Correct the timing detail: segment 73 (the twin heavy-tail argument) follows the first FAIR-bounded estate pricing segment by roughly 8 minutes, not forty — the whole pitch-v6 video runs about 20 minutes total, so "forty minutes of estate beats" is not physically possible in this cut. Restate as something like "immediately after the estate segments priced by the bounded engine" or "~8 minutes after the FAIR pricing segments begin," without the forty-minute figure.

findings.title: The institutions' risk appetite and their threat pricing are authored by the platform, in the platform's repo
findings.claim: All four appetite bands live in one file in the platform repository and the adopters carry read-only mirrors whose verify scripts fail if they differ, and the threat register that prices each institution is a dict literal in the platform's own source — yet the pitch narrates the resulting decisions as made by numbers each institution published itself.
findings.evidence: platform/risk/appetite.json holds driftwood 40000, tuppence 15000, ludlow 5000, platform 10000. ludlow/verify-reconcile.sh:45-46 and tuppence/verify-reconcile.sh:45-46 read the platform file and fail if the org's configmap differs; ludlow/gitops/apps/risk-appetite-configmap.yaml:9-13 — "platform/risk/appetite.json remains the single source of truth". platform/feeds/to_fair_scenario.py:33-38 — THREAT_LM_GBP per institution, hardcoded in the platform. pitch-v6 narration segment 30 — "The money decided, using numbers each of them published themselves"; segment 15 — "Against the retailer's published appetite". The same deck opens with "Nobody here can reach into anybody else's repository, and no credential spans them."
findings.recommendation: Move each institution's tolerance into its own party.yaml, signed under its own release tag, and make platform read it as an inherited declaration rather than own it. The mirrors and drift checks already exist, pointing the wrong way. It is the difference between an eco-system and a monorepo with six directories.

findings.title: The twin built the actuarial additions and dropped the FAIR skeleton they were meant to sit on, and three of them are wired to nothing
findings.claim: twin research 02 specified keeping the FAIR skeleton and adding Hubbard calibration, empirical heavy-tail anchoring and Buhlmann credibility; the additions were built as standalone CLI verbs and the skeleton was dropped, so the twin's own GBP path (pricing.py -> tradeoff.py) contains no frequency, no Monte Carlo, no TVaR, no anchored severity and no credibility blend.
findings.evidence: Specified: "keep the FAIR skeleton (LEF x LM -> PERT leaves -> Monte-Carlo -> loss-exceedance curve; Open FAIR, not a vendor black box) and add calibrated estimation (Hubbard), empirical heavy-tailed anchoring (Cyentia IRIS / DBIR / NetDiligence; lognormal body + Pareto/GPD tail), credibility theory (Buhlmann-Straub)" (twin research 02, per INVENTORY.json). Built: twin/pricing.py imports admission, corroboration, evidence, options, propagate, artefact, canon, pert — not severity, not anchoring, not credibility; grep across twin/*.py shows those three reached only from verbs.py as separate commands. pricing.py:118-124 and :318-321 state no re-sampling happens in pricing by design. The twin-risk-engine code map records the same split: "credibility.py is a separate Bayesian-blending capability not wired into pricing.py in this file set".
findings.recommendation: Wire one of the three into the price path — credibility.blend() on the valuation triple is smallest and most defensible, being exactly the world-prior/own-data blend the world/overlay split was designed around. Whatever stays unwired should be labelled in does_not_do.py as a standalone capability rather than presented as part of "the FAIR engine".
corrections:
Minor nuance, not a refutation: pricing.py frames the missing severity slot as a considered design decision (build ticket 30 / decision ticket 09) rather than an accidental drop. The finding's core claim — spec called for keeping the FAIR skeleton and wiring in the three additions; what was built is three standalone unwired verbs plus a GBP price path with no frequency, Monte Carlo, TVaR, anchored severity, or credibility blend — is accurate as stated.</parameter>
</invoke>

Severity/anchoring/credibility being unwired from the GBP price path is a documented, deliberate outcome of decision ticket 09 (which rejected the "shadow price" / two-authored-magnitude shape research-02 had sketched), not a dropped skeleton — pricing.py's own docstring names this as "a decision rather than an omission." Separately, the claim that the GBP path contains no Monte Carlo is factually wrong: propagate.py, which pricing.py imports and depends on, is the system's Monte-Carlo engine (PERT triples, per-trial draws, sampled spread), and pricing.py deliberately avoids re-sampling only to prevent double-counting uncertainty already sampled upstream. At most there is a legitimate, much narrower observation left standing: severity/anchoring/credibility exist as standalone CLI verbs and are not blended into a price figure — but that is a known, named, decision-backed design choice, not "drift," and does not support "no Monte Carlo... in the twin's own GBP path."

findings.title: No estimate in either engine has been calibration-tested, and no priced figure has ever been scored against an outcome the project did not author
findings.claim: Every triple in both engines is hand-authored with no recorded elicitation; the twin's Hubbard-style calibration procedure is enforced only as a regex check that a markdown file still contains five named step ids; and the one instrument aimed at external reality has never scored a resolution.
findings.evidence: Estate: eleven scenario fixtures in total, nine of them driftwood's or the platform's own, all hand-authored — the estate code map's own words: "no estimate here comes from an elicitation process or a real actuarial source". Twin: every org is a fixtures.py synthetic named after a real company (Carillion, NMC Health, Wirecard, Enron, Netflix, Royal Mail, Intel, Kodak, Maersk). twin/calibration.md is a real 5-step Hubbard procedure but pert.procedure() enforces it by requiring the five step ids to match by regex and returning a sha256 pin — no estimator is named, no interval is scored, no overconfidence is measured anywhere in the repo. twin/benchmark.py:361-364 — "this suite reaches no live venue", so proportionality_verdict()'s resolved list is empty in every real run. The only empirically anchored numbers in the project are the two cited Cyentia IRIS 2025 quantiles in twin/severity-anchors.yaml, for one subject, in a module the price path does not call.
findings.recommendation: Run the calibration procedure on the actual author for the ten triples that drive the demo, and record estimator, date and interval width in the scenario files so a later back-test can score them. A day's work, and it converts "the numbers are hand-authored" from an admission into a method.
corrections: The claim should be narrowed to: the forecast-book benchmark suite (twin/benchmark.py, twin/market_signals.py) has never scored a live-venue resolution — that part is accurate and documented in the module's own docstring. But it is false that no priced figure has ever been scored against an unauthored outcome: twin/verbs.py's score() plus the Carillion/NMC/Wirecard/Royal Mail/Enron backtest fixtures in twin/fixtures.py constitute a second, working instrument that does exactly this, exercised by a passing test (tests/test_carillion.py::test_a_carillion_forecast_scores_against_the_resolved_answer_key). The calibration-procedure-as-regex-check claim is accurate and survives.

findings.title: The insurance and risk-transfer half the owner asked to be folded in was reduced to a flat 40% load, and no counterparty exists
findings.claim: The owner asked for traditional insurance practice to be folded in and the balance sheet proved comprehensively under a no-nice-to-haves rule; what shipped is a single scalar tolerance per org, an expected-loss premium with a guessed load, no attachment point, no limit, no exclusions, and no insurer or broker among the six parties.
findings.evidence: Owner 2026-07-23: "Are there traditional insurance practices we should use/reference" -> "Fold in"; "go deep on the balance sheet ... proved comprehensively"; "nothing is a nice to have". DECISION_AUDIT P177 records the assistant's own framing offering cyber-policy structure (limits, retentions, exclusions) as an optional extra and the owner's reply taking "the cheapest of three options offered"; verdict recorded as reverse. Built: platform/risk/appetite.json carries one scalar "tolerance" per org; tcor.py:57-61 DEFAULT_LOAD 0.40 self-described as a mid-range guess; tcor.py:111 premium = ale_warn x (1 + load); party roles across the six repos are publisher / risk-bearer / adopter only.
findings.recommendation: Give the appetite object an attachment point, a limit and an exclusion list, and price transfer off TVaR between attachment and limit. Then add a seventh party publishing a signed quote for those terms. That is the shape in which a priced cage is bought and compared, and it is what makes the feeds marketplace an economy rather than a distribution channel.

findings.title: Currency is not modelled: a USD penalty triple and a GBP one are summed as if identical, and the twin has no currency field at all
findings.claim: ico's penalty schema declares a currency per regime and the multi-obligation converter ignores it, producing a single loss-magnitude list mixing dollars and pounds which fair.py sums and reports as GBP; on the twin side no amount carries a currency anywhere, while the only empirically anchored figures in the project are USD.
findings.evidence: Reproduced here 2026-08-27: `python3 ico/schema/to_fair_scenario.py build v2/penalty-schema.json uk-gdpr higher-tier --also hipaa:willful-neglect-uncorrected` emits warn.lm = [[12700000, 18400000, 24000000], [68928, 2067813, 2067813]] — the first GBP (ICO monetary penalty notices), the second USD (45 CFR 160.404 tiers) — with a note saying only "priced additively and correlated". fair.py:78-88 sums them; every downstream string prints "GBP". lm_triple() branches on currency only to pick a dict key, never to convert. Twin: grep for a currency field across twin/*.py and *.yaml finds the word only in prose and a capability name; twin/severity-anchors.yaml amounts are USD (Cyentia IRIS 2025, $600k median / $32M p95) feeding twin/severity.py, whose docstring line 3 calls it "the GBP's TVaR-over-VaR commitment".
findings.recommendation: Put a currency on the amount, not on the regime: refuse to combine sources of different currencies unless a dated, versioned FX rate is supplied as another signed feed. The refusal is three lines and is more convincing on stage than a conversion would be — the same refuse-rather-than-default discipline the twin enforces everywhere else.
corrections: Narrow finding to the ico-schema and fair.py mechanism, which is verified and material. Soften claim that fair.py prints GBP everywhere (only cage.py does) and that twin has no currency concept (the twin's currency symbol is a documented abstract pricing unit, not an oversight).

findings.title: "Risk on the balance sheet" is one hand-authored portfolio for one org, printed to stdout
findings.claim: The balance-sheet strand the owner asked to be proved comprehensively exists as a three-risk fixture book for driftwood only, nothing maps a running workload to a scenario, and no GBP figure in the estate is rendered anywhere except a terminal.
findings.evidence: tcor/scenarios/driftwood-portfolio.json is the only portfolio in the estate (46 lines, three risks, hand-set fix/deny/transfer costs). .scratch/computed-semver/map.md:228-231 — "the estate holds two FAIR scenarios in total, both driftwood's. Nothing maps a pod to a scenario ... the cage half of the model is proved on synthetic input until it exists." The estate code map's closing note: "no number is displayed anywhere but stdout". The owner's 2026-07-16 ask was a CIO dashboard; the 2026-07-23 ask was "technological risk on the balanace sheet of the business".
findings.recommendation: Give each institution a portfolio file in its own repo, built by mapping running workloads to scenarios via the posture label the cage already stamps, and render the roll-up as one committed markdown table per release. The engine exists; what is missing is one join and one view.

findings.title: The appetite store still declares enforcement binary, months after the owner replaced the gate with cages
findings.claim: platform/risk/appetite.json's own note states that enforcement is binary Audit-versus-Deny and that crossing the band MUST escalate to Deny, and risk/PR.md still narrates that escalation as the money beat — neither was revisited after the owner's move to "there is no real gate anymore, just cages".
findings.evidence: platform/risk/appetite.json:2 — "Enforcement is binary here (Audit vs Deny): a control's residual risk-bought ... above the org's tolerance MUST escalate Audit->Deny". risk/PR.md:12-14,39-49 narrates the Audit->Deny escalation with a hand-written validationActions diff that PR.md:42-43 concedes "is hand-edited only to match what the number already decided". Owner 2026-08-22: "there is no real gate anymore. Just cages. That may ultimately degrade to something that is too expensive to run or not functional"; 2026-08-20: "you're always caged even if it's a permissive one. It's the spec of the cage that can change". graded/cage.py added the tier layer on top but kept Deny as its bottom rung and left the risk/ vocabulary untouched.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the appetite note and PR.md in cage vocabulary: the band does not flip a verdict, it selects a cage tier, and Deny is the tier at which the cage is too tight to run. cage.select_tier already implements exactly that; only the prose and the risk/ CLI's output vocabulary are behind.

duplications_and_contradictions: Two complete risk engines: .estate-clone/platform/fair/fair.py (FAIR, LEF x LM Monte Carlo -> ALE/VaR95/TVaR) and twin/pricing.py + tradeoff.py (perspectival valuation x propagated influence, point-wise, no frequency). Neither imports the other; the twin's spec calls its own stack 'the FAIR engine' while containing no LEF or ALE anywhere.

Two Buhlmann credibility implementations with different formulations: platform/honesty/calibration.py buhlmann() (portfolio EPV/VHM, k = EPV/VHM, over three orgs) and twin/credibility.py credibility_z() (K = own variance / world variance, single org against a world prior). Neither cites the other.

Two TVaR implementations: fair.py:112-115 (empirical mean of draws beyond the 95th percentile of a bounded distribution) and twin/severity.py:159-175 (closed-form McNeil & Frey over a GPD tail, refusing when VaR falls in the lognormal body). They are not comparable quantities.

Two beta-PERT samplers: fair.py:49-56 (rng.betavariate over [lo,hi]) and twin/pert.py:139-182 (analytic Beta moments plus a name-keyed seeded stream). Only the twin's is pinned to a calibration procedure.

Two feed-to-scenario converters with the same filename and forked logic: platform/feeds/to_fair_scenario.py (207 lines, threat/CVE/EOL) and ico/schema/to_fair_scenario.py (184 lines, penalty regimes). The platform copy's docstring acknowledges the fork ('Same shape as estate/ico/schema/to_fair_scenario.py'). Both invent their own editorial LEF.

The policy-composition standing preference 'No second risk engine, no second appetite store' (spec.md:247) is honoured scrupulously inside the estate — composition re-prices through ico's own converter, the feeds module, cage.select() and risk/appetite.json — and is silently violated at project scale by twin/, which the preference's own effort never mentions.

twin/spec.md Out of Scope declares 'the toy risk model' and 'The estate/ monorepo and the KinD clusters. Binned.' (2026-08-05), while the pitch built 2026-08-25 devotes roughly forty of its eighty-one segments to that same estate risk model and calls the twin 'one arm, not the whole body' (narration segment 57). Neither document was updated.

ico's penalty schema carries a percentage rate and a statutory cap per regime; the converter derives loss from other companies' published fines instead, so the schema's two most org-sensitive fields are inert while the file is presented as the mechanism by which a regulator's fine re-proportions an org's controls.

platform/honesty/README.md ('The incident log is a curated fixture, not a live SIEM feed') contradicts honesty/verify-honesty.sh:4,19 and pitch narration segment 45, both of which say 'real incidents', in the same directory.

graded/README.md presents the cage as the delivered mechanism while graded/up.sh:1-14 labels the apply path 'DEMO PATH, not delivery' with Flux out of the loop; graded/verify-graded.sh currently exits 1 on its live tail (kind-driftwood carries cage-tier-1-0-0 and 2-0-0 while distribution/versions.yaml declares 2.0.0/2.0.1/3.0.0).
oscal/verify-claims.sh:6-10 still narrates an EXPECTED-RED claim state that lint_claims.py:59-62 and the current green run superseded.
summary: The risk work is the most genuinely built part of the project and the most drifted from what the owner asked for. What exists is real: a deterministic seeded Monte-Carlo FAIR engine whose selfchecks all pass, an appetite band that selects a cage tier rather than an opinion, four risk-financing moves with a computed crossover, an OSCAL up-flow whose risk-to-observation join resolves by construction, a Buhlmann back-test, and — in the twin — a careful heavy-tailed severity model with two cited empirical quantiles and an honest declaration of the two parameters it cannot anchor. Almost every module names its own fixtures in its own README. That candour is the project's strongest asset and it is undercut in exactly the places an audience will look. Three things are critical. First, there are two risk engines answering different questions with no seam and no document acknowledging the second one; the estate's own rule against a second engine was written by an effort that never mentions the twin. Second, the owner's clearest and most recent correction — on 19 August, that a flat pound figure across differently-sized organisations is not credible and that loss should follow a percentage-of-global-revenue regulatory consequence — produced no specification, no code and no change to the demo, which still narrates the same figure for two institutions; the field that would carry it already sits unread in the ICO schema. Third, the flagship falsifiability beat back-tests the model against a file the project authored to produce that exact verdict, describes it as "real incidents" in both the verify script and the narration, reports the flattering half of the result, and compares a single privileged operation's exposure against an entire organisation's loss history. Beneath those, the pattern is consistent: the sophisticated parts are computed and then not used. VaR95, TVaR, economic capital and the Solvency-II risk load are calculated and consumed by nothing; every decision is made on the mean of a bounded distribution that cannot express a tail event, in a system whose other half rejected a rival technology for precisely that flaw. The recalibration factor is computed and applied to nothing. The heavy-tail severity, the empirical anchor and the credibility blend are three standalone commands the twin's own price path never calls. Nothing is fetched, nothing is scheduled, nothing has been calibration-tested, and no priced figure in either engine has ever been scored against an outcome the project did not author. The owner said his thinking evolved "around risk assessment was done and what we modelled" — the honest answer is that the modelling machinery is real and well-tested, and every number that goes into it is one the project wrote for itself.

findings.title: The composed policy set never reaches a cluster in any of the three institutions
findings.claim: Nothing in driftwood, tuppence or ludlow applies composed/policies/** to a Kubernetes cluster: each institution's Flux Kustomization reconciles only ./apps, whose kustomization.yaml lists a namespace and two ConfigMaps, and the ResourceSet fan-out that would install policy versions is opt-in and has never been applied.

Apply it once the cluster has its prerequisites". driftwood/gitops/apps/version-configmap.yaml:8-11 declares itself a Phase-0 marker standing in for the real policy set. The composed trees (composed/policies/{v2.0.0,v2.0.1,v3.0.0}/*.yaml, composed/orphan-guard.yaml, composed/governed-namespace-guard.yaml) are committed YAML with no consumer.
findings.recommendation: Wire gitops/platform into the Phase-0 reconcile for at least one institution and make composed/ the thing the ResourceSet installs, or state plainly in every artefact and in the deck that composition is a merge-time artefact and enforcement is not demonstrated. This is the single joint whose absence makes the eco-system undemonstrable end to end: everything upstream of admission is real and nothing downstream of it is.

findings.title: The regulator is consumed from a moving branch: ico is neither pinned, versioned nor verified on any composition edge
findings.claim: Every adopter's compose job checks ico out at `ref: main`, and composition resolves the ico pricing edge by running `git log -1` over a version subdirectory rather than from a signed tag, so one of the four parent edges recorded in every composed artefact has no pin, no signature check and no Renovate route — in the one party the owner named as the reason regulators are upstream dependencies.
findings.evidence: driftwood/.github/workflows/shift-left.yml (compose-check job) checks out policy-as-versioned-platform/platform at ${{ steps.pins.outputs.platform_tag }} and policy-as-versioned-nist/nist at the nist tag, but policy-as-versioned-ico/ico with `ref: main`; identical in tuppence and ludlow. platform/compose/composition.py:269-315 resolve_sha(): only (party,kind) pairs in party_artefact.PIN_FILES read a Flux pin; pricing and threat fall through to _resolve_unpinned_sha, which is `git log -1 --format=%H -- <version dir>` or, failing that, a content digest. driftwood/party.yaml's own comment: "`pricing` and `threat` have no Flux pin anywhere in this estate today". ico ships one tag, v1.0.0, and no adopter has a gotk-sync-ico.yaml. .scratch/multi-org-estate/issues/07-split-mechanics-decision.md: "nobody pins `ico` as a GitRepository at all". Owner 2026-07-23: "the ico might be able to publish a machine readable financial penalty" — as a versioned artefact like a lint pack.
findings.recommendation: Give ico the same treatment as nist: a signed semver tag per schema version, a gotk-sync-ico.yaml pin in each institution, a Renovate customManager on it, and a compose-time checkout at the pinned tag. This is also the cheapest way to make the feeds-marketplace story concrete, since ico is the estate's only regulator-published price feed.

findings.title: The regulator-derived £ is identical across all three institutions, the figure shape the owner rejected
findings.claim: Every composed evidence.json prices the ico edge at exactly £16,901,471.55 for driftwood, tuppence and ludlow, because composition hardcodes one regime/violation pair and the loss-magnitude triple is derived from other companies' published fines rather than from the adopter's own size — the same flat-figure-per-org shape the owner rejected on 2026-08-19.

Note the threat edge DOES vary per org (£19,558 / £222,574 / £318,230) — the machinery can differentiate; the regulator edge is the one that does not.

This is a small change that removes the exact criticism the owner made of the v5 deck.

findings.title: Multi-regulator and customer-SLA obligations are built in the publisher and bound to no institution
findings.claim: ico's schema carries pci-dss and hipaa regimes and its converter supports folding several regimes into one correlated scenario, and mo-18 made fair.py accept a list of loss magnitudes — yet ludlow (declared US health / HIPAA) and tuppence (declared FCA + PCI + GDPR) both compose only uk-gdpr/lower-tier, and no customer-SLA artefact exists anywhere in the estate.

findings.title: The COTS shim was decided four times and built zero times, and the shipped cage explicitly excludes the population it was meant to cover

findings.title: Dual signing was decided and silently reversed; no cluster verifies any signature and no party verifies another party's artefact tag
findings.claim: mo-07 resolved that tags would be dual-signed (gitsign + per-org OpenPGP keys held as org secrets, time-boxed until Flux ships gitsign) so `GitRepository.spec.verify` would bite at the cluster; no OpenPGP signature or spec.verify block exists anywhere, every gotk-sync.yaml states the opposite decision in a comment, and the only cross-party signature verification in the estate is the adopter gate's cosign check of platform's evidence document — never of a policy artefact tag.

Keys are per-org, held as GitHub Actions org secrets, backed up to the owner's 1Password vault... This is a bridge, not a design choice." Against that: driftwood/gitops/flux-system/gotk-sync.yaml:7 "GitRepository.spec.verify only speaks OpenPGP, so we do NOT fake a PGP block here" (identical in tuppence, ludlow and the nist sync files). `grep -rn 'spec.verify|openpgp|dual sign'` across all six repos returns only comments — no key, no secretRef, no verify: block. driftwood/.github/workflows/release.yml:76-86 gitsign verify-tag runs only on the repo's own tag push. The one real cross-party verification is driftwood/.github/scripts/adopter-gate.py:254-264 `cosign verify-blob --certificate-identity-regexp` against platform's release-gate evidence. Owner 2026-08-20: "3 dual sign, seed private keys for each org, and only needs to exist until flux supports gitsign which is in their roadmap".
findings.recommendation: Either implement the bridge the owner chose (per-org OpenPGP key as an org secret, dual-signed tag, spec.verify on each GitRepository, with a link to the upstream Flux gitsign issue so removal is triggerable), or record an ADR reversing mo-07 with the reasoning. Right now a resolved decision and the shipped code say opposite things with no decision record between them, and the pitch's 'signed dependencies exchanged between six orgs' claim rests on a check no consumer performs.
corrections: none -- original claim confirmed as stated

findings.title: The six orgs are a CI fact, never a runtime fact: clusters still reconcile from an in-cluster git server seeded from the local tree
findings.claim: Each institution's up.sh seeds its gitops/ tree into a throwaway repo inside a busybox git-http-backend image loaded into KinD and points Flux at http://git-server.flux-system.svc.cluster.local, so no cluster in the estate has ever reconciled from a real policy-as-versioned-* GitHub remote; mo-09 still carries Status: partial and the committed gotk-sync.yaml pins v1.0.0 with its commit line commented out while v1.1.0 (the composed-artefact release) exists.

Real signed tags v1.1.0 now exist in all three institutions (`git cat-file -p v1.1.0` shows real Sigstore certs), so the blocker named in the ticket is gone and the pin was never advanced. Owner 2026-08-19: "2 split everything. We are demonstrating a multi org thing"; 2026-07-23: "they should all be fully live".

One cluster reconciling from a real signed cross-org remote converts the multi-org claim from a CI artefact into a demonstrable one, and it is the prerequisite for the composed set ever being enforced (H9-01).

findings.title: A second, live implementation of the same thesis is still running in the hub org, and it is the only place the version fan-out actually reaches a cluster

Against INVENTORY.json's record that docs/ARCHIVE.md declares the hub "superseded, research-only, no further feature work" with the archive checklist NOT DONE. Leaving both live means any live demo of 'policy versions installing on a cluster' is a demo of the superseded implementation.

findings.title: The party/role registry a marketplace needs is a single hub-owned file, and its guard passes on a text match

findings.title: The version array's commit pins are deliberately one commit behind the signed tags, and the adopters' pin files describe the opposite rule
findings.claim: platform/distribution/versions.yaml pins each policy version to the evidence commit, which verify-publisher-gate.sh asserts must be the tag's resolved commit's direct parent, while driftwood/gitops/platform/platform-pin.yaml and its ADR-0001 reference describe the commit field as 'the resolved SHA the tag points to' — two incompatible readings of the same field, never tested because no cluster has applied the ResourceSet.
findings.evidence: platform/distribution/versions.yaml pins 2.0.0 and 3.0.0 to fa862b710fe34b475aba54f926a95164f003b0c1 and 2.0.1 to a1072d9e183ca06a9aaf626d25869996e6179695; `git rev-list -n1` resolves policy/v2.0.0 and policy/v3.0.0 to e34ae7f5 and policy/v2.0.1 to ebc4ff5c; fa862b71 is e34ae7f5's direct parent. platform/verify-publisher-gate.sh:255-263 makes this an invariant: "versions.yaml's `commit` field for the cut version equals the EVIDENCE commit (commit A) — one commit BEHIND the tag it actually resolves to (commit B)" and fails if the two are equal. driftwood/gitops/platform/platform-pin.yaml:26-30: "commit pinned at release (belt-and-braces immutability, ADR-0001) -- the resolved SHA platform v1.1.0 tag points to" (also stale: the tag on the line above is v1.1.1). findings.recommendation: Pick one meaning for the field and state it in ADR-0001. If Flux is ever to reconcile this ResourceSet, `ref.tag` + `ref.commit` must agree with the tag, which means the array-correction commit has to be inside the tag; if the parent-commit invariant is deliberate, the field should be named something other than the Flux pin's `commit`.
corrections: Not a contradiction between two readings of one field — it's two different fields (platform's internal policy-version pin vs. an adopter's pin to the platform release itself) in different manifests, each independently tested and documented as intentional. Not confirmed as owner-evolution-not-propagated. ADR-0016, dated after both cited owner quotes, explicitly considered and rejected making restatement strictness a position on the cage-spec/tier lattice (the finding's own recommendation), on grounds consistent with the owner's priced-cage model (tier is a £-priced verdict, not an overlay declaration) and Kyverno schema limits. The owner's "no gate, just cages" evolution was propagated via the tier/proposer mechanism (ADR-0015/0016), just not by changing the Audit/Deny ladder, which serves a narrower and still-valid purpose for ValidatingPolicy rules.

The STRICTNESS={Audit:0,Deny:1} ladder and cages[]=[] observations are accurate, but the finding's central claim — that this is unpropagated owner-evolution rather than a deliberate choice — is contradicted by ADR-0016 (2026-08-25), which explicitly considers and rejects feeding the cage lattice into composition's restatement check, for reasons tied to who is allowed to set a priced verdict. The "there is no real gate anymore. Just cages" quote is not a real verbatim citation; the real 2026-08-22 text is in a different ticket (computed-semver cs-07) discussing a different set of policies.

summary: The publishing half of the eco-system is real and the consuming half is not. Six independent GitHub organisations exist, cut genuinely gitsign-signed tags from real Actions runs, and exchange artefacts through real cross-org CI; composition.py and the computed-semver seam are substantial, honest, self-checking code that runs on every pull request in all three institutions and passes nine of eleven verify scripts on this machine. What is missing is every joint that would make it an operating eco-system rather than a set of well-formed documents. No composed policy reaches a cluster — the institutions reconcile a namespace and two ConfigMaps, and the ResourceSet fan-out is opt-in and unapplied. The three institutions' composed enforcement is byte-identical apart from a label, so the owner-ratified money shot (same control, Audit in driftwood, Deny in ludlow) is produced not by composition but by a separate hub-side renderer for a control that does not exist in the estate. The OO half of "inherit from others and mash up" has zero live instances: every overlay, restatement, cage, adopter control claim and diamond refusal is empty or fixture-only. Computed semver has never computed a bump — all three signed evidence documents record 'none' against a hand-declared number, and the per-institution matrix is {}. The regulator is consumed from `ref: main`, unpinned and unverified, and prices every institution at the same £16.9M, the exact figure shape the owner rejected on 2026-08-19. The COTS shim was decided four times and built zero times, and the shipped cage explicitly excludes the unversioned population it was meant to cover, against "nothing runs without a cage". Dual signing was decided and silently reversed. The minimal missing joints, in order: (1) apply one institution's composed set to its cluster via the ResourceSet; (2) give one institution a real overlay — a restatement and a priced cage — so composition differs per party; (3) pin ico as a signed versioned dependency and bind each institution's actual regulators; (4) cut one release whose number the gate determines. Those four would make the eco-system demonstrable end to end; today it is demonstrable as a supply chain of signed documents, not as a system that governs anything.
